CB01-4: Member Input Policy Summary Chapter meetings provide a regular opportunity for members to gather and discuss political issues, as well as solutions we can provide as a socialist organization. This political discussion, however, is not uniformly shared across the organization. The member input plank aims to foster simultaneous discussion within chapters and across the country, building a sense of belonging to a shared national organization beyond the local level. Full text The NPC will recommend topics or questions for discussion by chapters on a regular basis, at least four times a year. The topics are recommended for discussion by chapters at their next general meeting or a meeting organized for the purpose of that discussion. The recommended discussion topic will be publicized by membership-wide communication, through the DSA website and forums, and by email to chapters and chapter co-chairs of record. NPEC, or any other body delegated by the NPC, will assist with chapter communication, compiling materials and facilitation guides, and hosting events as needed. Votes on resolutions are encouraged, and resolution text shall be reported to the NPC, including language of the resolution and vote total results. Results of votes will be published to all members. The NPC will give a report to the next convention on participation in these discussions. There are no significant financial costs, as the resolution relies on existing communication platforms, volunteer labor, and internal resources. CB01-5: National Commission Policy Summary This plank standardizes types of national working bodies (commissions and working groups) and elections for their leadership, establishes transparency requirements, and centralizes applications and onboarding. It builds in a process for handling administrative matters for working bodies at Convention, ensuring regular member oversight. Full text DSA Policy on National Working Bodies All DSA national committees, commissions, working groups, and any NPC subcommittee or national DSA working body open to members other than the National Political Committee and DSA staff (hereafter, working bodies) will have one of two structures: * Appointed committees: Appointed committees will have a fixed number of members, set either by the NPC or by the National Convention, and appointed by the NPC or by the National Convention following an open application period of at least a month. The requirements for membership and specific method of appointment are left to the discretion of the NPC or the National Convention, but all valid applicants must be considered. * Open commissions: Open commissions may have an unbounded number of members, and applications to a commission must be processed at least four times a year. Requirements to participate in a commission may be set by the NPC, the National Convention, or the commission itself, but all applicants who fulfill the requirements must be accepted. Applications to a commission will be processed by the commission’s Steering Committee, or by a subcommittee within the commission to which the task is specifically delegated. Open commissions will be one of the following types: * Standing Commission: Ongoing, permanent bodies organized around key functional or strategic areas * Working Groups: Time-limited or project-specific bodies organized around discrete tasks, campaigns, or initiatives which are dissolved once their work is complete All working bodies must be open to application by DSA members in good standing, and all applications for working bodies will be consolidated into a single application, which will be linked on the “Working Groups” and “Get Involved” pages of the DSA website and on the DSA forums. Members must remain in good standing to participate in national committees. Commission leadership (and any members who handle member or financial data in the course of their work) must sign data usage agreements and have those on file with national staff. Associations Members may form Associations, which is a lightweight recognized status for groups of members who share a common interest, identity, or focus. Associations are not DSA working bodies and should not generally be assigned externally-facing campaign work by the NPC or Convention, but the NPC or Convention may pass a charter converting an association into a working body in order to take on externally-facing work. Associations may be formed one of two ways: * Members may seek recognition from the NPC showing that 15+ members have been meeting for at least three months * Open commissions that are being dechartered for inactivity may be converted into associations by the NPC if 15+ members of the group request it The NPC may exercise oversight of associations if necessary, but associations will not have liaising assignments or other ongoing use of NPC or staff time. Associations will be given a section of the DSA Forums. They cannot submit budget requests to the national organization. Associations with no proof of activity or discussion in their forum section for 6 months will be closed. Associations may not create websites, social media, pamphlets, or any other such outwardly facing materials construed as representing DSA or official opinions of the organization. Chartering, Renewal, and Dechartering All working bodies must be chartered by a vote of the NPC or Convention. All resolutions establishing a working body should specify the intended duration of their work, which may be in perpetuity, and a working body will close after two years of operation if no duration is specified, unless reauthorized by the National Convention or NPC. Before each National Convention the NPC will prepare a report on the status of all working bodies active during their term, due on the initial deadline of member-submitted resolutions to the Convention. The report will include each working body charter, a brief summary of funding and any other notable institutional resources provided, and level of activity. It will also list any working bodies dechartered during the term for any reason. The NPC will vote on recommendations for the next term, whether to recharter, decharter, combine, or otherwise amend their status, and any amendments to their membership or structure. Members may propose amendments to these recommendations through the regular resolution process. Changes to membership and structure of working bodies will be proposed through this process. The report will be considered by the Convention, where delegates may amend recommendations on working bodies before voting on the package as a whole to approve the status of all working bodies for the next term. Despite otherwise being governed by rules governing amendments to resolutions proposed to the Convention, amendments to the working body report may be placed on the consent agenda and are eligible for secondary amendment. Records All working bodies must have a designated secretary responsible for maintaining minutes that reflect decisions made, including voting totals. Any votes conducted asynchronously (such as via Loomio, group chats, or other non-meeting motions) must be ratified at the next standing meeting of that body, using records maintained by the secretary. Any decision requiring action outside of a body’s official meetings must be automatically placed on the agenda for the next standing meeting of that body. Working bodies using asynchronous voting must establish a method and timeline for asynchronous voting, established as a standing rule by a two-thirds majority vote of the body. Working body records should be available to members in the DSA meeting minutes archive and policy library, updated at least quarterly, unless the NPC votes to make an exception for security reasons. All working body records must be made available to the NPC upon request. Any decision-making body that fails to maintain or provide its records may have its secretary replaced by the NPC or may be subject to dechartering by the NPC or the DSA National Convention. Complete lists of members of appointed committees and NPC subcommittees will be made available to DSA members in good standing in a central membership-only site. A list of active associations will additionally be maintained and available to membership. These will be updated on at least an annual basis. Steering Committees All open commissions must have a Steering Committee approved by the NPC, including at minimum a secretary and a chair or co-chairs. Steering Committees for commissions will have a term of office no longer than two years, and will be selected as follows: 1. The membership of the commission will select a slate for the Steering Committee by Scottish Single Transferable Vote. All members of the commission will be permitted to vote in this election, and all members of the commission will be eligible to run for Steering Committee. Candidates for a commission’s Steering Committee must indicate whether they additionally intend to seek appointment as secretary, chair, co-chair, or other specific officer positions within the Steering Committee. 2. The National Political Committee will approve, amend, or replace the slate. The specific method of appointment is left to the discretion of the NPC, but information on all of the candidates must be made available to the full NPC. The NPC may designate the commission’s officers, or authorize the new Steering Committee to determine officer assignments among themselves. 3. If the NPC cannot decide on the commission’s Steering Committee in the meeting at which the commission-selected leadership slate is debated, then the Steering Committee will be selected by a proportional method by the NPC, and officer roles within the commission determined by the new Steering Committee. Existing national bodies will be classified according to these categories, and renamed and restructured accordingly, with the primary criterion for classification being the manner in which working body membership is determined: bodies appointed by the NPC should be classified as “committees” and bodies open to the general membership as “commissions.” Capacity Commitment & Financial Impact Scores Capacity 2: Low to Moderate Finances 1: Less than $5000 This recommendation establishes a comprehensive and standardized structure for all DSA national working bodies, including committees, commissions, working groups, and associations, defining how they are formed, governed, renewed, and dissolved. It introduces formalized processes for elections, asynchronous voting, record-keeping, and reporting, and requires the NPC to produce a detailed working body status report before each convention. Additionally, it mandates centralized archiving of records, standardized application systems, and restructuring of existing bodies, all of which require moderate to high staff coordination and member involvement, particularly during implementation and ongoing maintenance, justifying a Capacity Commitment score of 3. There are no significant financial costs, as the resolution relies on member labor, existing digital infrastructure, and internal administrative processes, resulting in a Financial Impact score of 1. CB01-9: Reauthorizing the Democracy Commission Summary This plank renews the charter of the Democracy Commission for another two years, with the explicit purpose of implementing the reforms proposed by the commission. Full text Whereas: * About 5.2% of the vote is disproportionately misallocated by the current convention delegate apportionment system. * The current delegate system distorts chapter representation at convention by introducing significant amounts of rounding errors. The current system is not proportional and creates unintuitive and irrational incentives for chapters by encouraging membership recruitment in arbitrary increments of 60 people at a time. * The current delegate system distorts chapter representation by giving members different amounts of effective voting power depending on what chapter they are in. In the most extreme cases at the current apportionment ratio, chapter apportionment ranges from 1 delegate per 89 members to 1 delegate per 9 members. This means that some members can have about 10 times as much effective voting power at convention when compared to other members simply because of where they are located. * All chapters would benefit from establishing a more proportional and transparent delegate apportionment system, in which there would be a more consistent and linear relationship between recruiting more members and getting more representation at Convention. Chapter delegates will be entitled to a number of votes equal to the number of votes their chapter is entitled to, divided by the number of delegates apportioned to their chapter, then rounded to one decimal place. Apportionment of delegates shall reflect the one-member, one-vote principle, as shall be ordered by the NPC within the guidelines set forth in the Bylaws. However, all Chapters shall be entitled to at least one delegate. Apportionment of delegates for a Special Convention will be identical to apportionment for the most recent regularly scheduled National Convention. Section 5. No election for delegates to the a regularly scheduled National Convention shall be held more than four months, or less than forty-five days, prior to the opening of the National Convention. No election for delegates shall be conducted before the apportionment of delegates according to Section 3 of this Article. All Chapter elections of delegates shall be by secret ballot. Election of delegates may be by proportional representation within the conditions prescribed in the Bylaws. Elections for delegates to a Special Convention must be held at the earliest availability of Chapters following their receipt of a call for a Special Convention. Chapters may opt to send the same slate of delegates as were sent to the most recent regularly scheduled National Convention, or to elect a new delegation according to the processes used to elect delegates to the most recent regularly scheduled National Convention. Section 7. Calls to the National Convention shall be issued by the NPC at least one-hundred (100) days prior to the opening date of the Convention. Calls to Special Conventions shall be issued by the petition calling such Convention, providing that the date is set between thirty (30) and sixty (60) days from the issuing of the call. National Political Committee as soon as possible upon the receipt of a valid petition, which must be no more than thirty (30) days following the receipt of the petition. The Special Convention will take place thirty (30) days after the call is issued. DSA Bylaws, Article VI. National Conventions Section 2. Elections for at-large delegates shall be conducted by the NPC. A call for candidates for at-large delegates shall be sent to all at-large members not less than three months and not more than five months prior to the opening date of the a regularly scheduled Convention, or as soon as possible upon receipt of a valid petition for a Special Convention. Two months prior to the a regularly scheduled Convention a ballot containing the names of the delegate candidates shall be sent to at-large members, or two weeks after receipt of a valid petition for a Special Convention. This ballot shall contain instructions regarding the number of delegates to be elected, voting procedures, and date for the counting of ballots. Ballots shall be counted at the National Office one month prior to the a regularly scheduled Convention, or one week after the ballots are sent in the event of a Special Convention. No more than one-half (½) of the available positions for at-large delegates may be available to men and one-fifth (⅕) of the available positions (all genders) must be reserved for members who identify as either a nationally marginalized race or ethnicity. Those candidates who have been elected shall be immediately informed of their election by the National Office. With the exception of the shortened timeline, the processes used to elect at-large delegates to a Special Convention should be the same as those used to elect at-large delegates to the most recent regularly scheduled National Convention. Section 5. Regularly-scheduled National Conventions shall be held in a location decided on by the NPC at least a year in advance of the convention, while continuing our practice of only patronizing union-staffed hotels or convention sites. Special Conventions shall be held virtually. Section 6. Special Conventions may each consider only one resolution, which must be included in the petition for the Special Convention, and amendments to that resolution, which must be submitted to the National Political Committee at least a week in advance of the Special Convention with a number of signatures from DSA members in good standing equal to at least one-tenth () the number of apportioned delegates. Special Conventions may not alter DSA’s Constitution or Bylaws. Section 7. Special Conventions may elect a new National Political Committee if the recall of the current National Political Committee is included in the Special Convention petition. The new National Political Committee will serve the remainder of the prior National Political Commitee’s term and will be elected with the same procedures used to elect the prior National Political Committee, except that any member in good standing with a number of nominating signatures from other members in good standing equal to at least one-twentieth () the number of the apportioned delegates may be a candidate. Section 8. A pending petition for a Special Convention is rendered void if it fails to reach either endorsement threshold specified in Article V, Section 2 of the DSA Constitution at least three months prior to the next regularly scheduled National Convention. CR01: Democracy Commission DSA National & Chapter Affiliation Agreement Proposal Submitted by Aaron B (Southeast MN), Connell H (River Valley), Ramsin C (Chicago), Allison K (New York City), Kristian H (North Texas). Qualified on Apr 23, 2025, with 519 signatures as of May 11, 2025. Status: Adopted Summary Once put into operation by the bylaws changes in CB01, this resolution establishes the chapter affiliation agreements for DSA. Along with expectations of chapters and national, this affiliation agreement establishes basic standards for DSA chapters. This includes a requirement for a minimum of one meeting per year with voting rights for all members in good standing, and a virtual discussion space for chapter members. It includes a requirement to have been in good standing for at least 30 days to vote for chapter leadership or convention delegates, or to be a chapter officer. Full text DSA National-Chapter Affiliation Agreement Preamble The purpose of this agreement is to ensure that the Democratic Socialists of America and its affiliated Chapters are working in partnership consistent with the organization’s democratic socialist principles, the policies of the organization, and in accordance with all applicable state and federal laws. While many of the practices addressed in this agreement are already commonplace within DSA, the intent of this agreement is to clearly define roles, responsibilities, and expectations for both DSA chapters and the National organization.

Section 1. Grant of Charter 1. Charter. DSA hereby grants CHAPTER a charter to be a local Chapter of the Democratic Socialists of America, conditioned on the terms and conditions of this Agreement. CHAPTER agrees to abide by this Agreement and all DSA governance documents, rules, policies, and procedures relating to Chapters as adopted in this agreement. 2. Territory. CHAPTER shall represent DSA as DSA’s local affiliate in the boundaries defined in its charter (the “Territory”), in accordance with DSA’s mission and purposes as set forth in DSA’s Constitution and Bylaws, all national policies, and this Agreement. DSA agrees that CHAPTER shall be the sole and exclusive Chapter of DSA in the Territory during the term of this agreement. CHAPTER agrees that, except as approved in writing by the Officers of DSA, DSA shall be the sole and exclusive national association representing the interest of the chapter. 3. Authorized Activities. DSA specifically authorizes CHAPTER to conduct activities within the Territory consistent with furthering the principles and values of democratic socialism, including but not limited to meetings, political education programs, local campaigns, fundraising, and all such other activities as directed by the National Convention or the NPC. 4. Prohibited Activities. CHAPTER agrees to refrain from any and all such activities that conflict with DSA’s democratic socialist principles, that violate federal, state or local law, and/or that could incur liability or harm to DSA, including but not limited to supporting, by contributing funds or otherwise, for-profit corporations or law enforcement, using organizational funds to purchase weapons of any kind, or direct disbursement of funds to individuals without approval from the General Membership.

Section 2. Duties of DSA DSA’s obligations to CHAPTER under this Agreement shall include: 1. Provide up to date lists of members within the Territory to CHAPTER on a weekly basis; 2. Provide regular and ongoing organizing support, training, and mentorship from, but not limited to, DSA staff; 3. Provide access to DSA’s suite of national organizing and tech tools, currently including Action Network, Spoke, Zoom, HubDialer, and VAN; 4. Provide access to DSA’s national training library as well as technical support in utilizing tech and organizing tools through DSA; 5. Preside over any and all national expulsion and grievance appeals pursuant to the procedures laid out in Resolution 33 and DSA’s Non-Resolution 33 Expulsions Process; 6. Notify CHAPTER of the chapter’s delegate apportionment for any and all DSA National Conventions. 7. Distribute the dues share to incorporated chapters, and maintain the debit cards of unincorporated chapters. 1. Dues share is set to: * 30% of the average monthly dues contribution from the first 50 chapter members * 25% of the average monthly dues share from the next 51-200 members * 20% of the next 201 members and up

Section 3. Duties of the Chapter 1. Governing Documents. CHAPTER agrees that its governing documents are and shall remain consistent in all material respects with DSA’s governing documents, and that in any conflict between the two, the national requirement shall prevail. 2. Leadership Elections. CHAPTER shall report the results of elections for officers and executive committee members, and of officers or executive committee members that have resigned or been removed within 30 days of any elections, appointments or changes. 3. Programs and Activities. CHAPTER shall endeavor to organize programs and activities to advance democratic socialism in the Territory. 4. Regular Contact. Chapter shall maintain regular contact with DSA on a monthly basis, through either meetings with elected NPC members, Field Organizers, or by attending monthly District Calls. 5. Compliance with Laws. CHAPTER warrants that it is, and shall remain, in full compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, and other legal standards. 6. Compliance with DSA. CHAPTER agrees to conduct its activities in full compliance with all DSA policies, procedures, and regulations, including mandates of the National Convention and NPC. 7. Recordkeeping, Reporting, and Inspection. CHAPTER shall maintain all records related to its corporate and tax-exempt status and shall forward to DSA copies of its Articles of Incorporation, Bylaws, and tax exemption correspondence from the Internal Revenue Service, as well as any adverse notices, requests for information by law enforcement, or other correspondence received from any governmental agency (e.g., Internal Revenue Service, state Secretary of State, or corresponding agency). CHAPTER shall maintain reasonable records related to all of its programs, activities, and operations. CHAPTER shall annually submit to DSA a copy of its most recently filed Form 990, Return of Organization Exempt from Income Tax, as submitted to the Internal Revenue Service, within 30 days of such filing. If required to file, upon the written request of DSA and at DSA’s expense, CHAPTER will permit DSA or DSA’s designated agent(s) to review appropriate records of CHAPTER pertaining to its programs, activities, and operations. Alternatively, CHAPTER shall send to DSA copies of such records upon the request of DSA. 8. Incorporation and Tax Status. CHAPTER warrants and represents that it is an incorporated nonprofit corporation, shall incorporate as a nonprofit corporation under state law within 6 months of the Effective Date of this Agreement, and/or that it will utilize DSA’s umbrella tax status if granted explicit permission by DSA. Further, CHAPTER warrants that it shall at all times be in good standing with its state of incorporation and operate in a manner consistent with CHAPTER’s tax-exempt purposes. Section 4. Standards of Democracy Chapters further agree to uphold the following standards in their practice of democracy. 1. Members must be in good standing for 30 days to vote in elections for Chapter-wide leadership, to hold Chapter-wide office, or to vote in elections for delegates to national convention. 2. Shall incorporate the national member code of conduct; 3. Shall require the holding of at least one general decision-making meeting on an annual basis. A decision-making meeting is defined as a meeting or section of a meeting run under the current edition of Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised or other parliamentary procedure authorized by chapter bylaws. The meetings are open to all members in good standing of the chapter who may propose business in order for it to be debated and voted upon. Decisions made at these meetings are binding at the chapter level. A delegated convention may count as one decision-making meeting in a year, provided delegates are directly elected by members in good standing through a proportional method. 4. That there shall be no higher decision-making body than a time-bounded General Meeting or Convention open to all members in good standing; 5. Branch Meetings shall have the following requirements 1. The meeting or section of the meeting runs under the current edition of Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised or other parliamentary procedure authorized by chapter bylaws. 2. The meetings are open to all members in good standing of the given territory of a branch, who may propose business in order for it to be debated and voted upon. Should meet quarterly 6. Shall require publishing to its members the Chapter’s budget at least on an annual basis; 7. Shall require use of a national service or system for the handling of internal election of its officers and convention delegates; 8. Shall require use of a national model form for the keeping of general meeting minutes and filing or reporting of those minutes. 9. A means for members to notify the NPC or national office in cases of non-compliance with Chapters Agreements. 10. Shall require an officer-level position for member engagement and orientation and political education, which can be a single officer or multiple officers; 11. Every chapter of DSA is required to have a common digital platform to facilitate intra-chapter communication. This may be a Slack, Discord, forum, or other presence where individuals can communicate with other members directly. Section 5. Amending the Chapter Charter The contents of the charter may only be amended at the National DSA Convention. Compliance with any new contents of the charter only applies after a renewal of charter. Section 6. Charter Term and Renewal The charter granted by DSA to CHAPTER shall become effective on the Effective Date set forth above and shall remain in full force and effect for up to two years, or until revoked by DSA or by CHAPTER in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement. 1. Charter application. The application to renew a chapter charter shall include the following items 1. If you would like to add zip codes please list them here 2. Current Chapter code of conduct and HGO process 3. Certificate of good standing if chapter is incorporated 4. If you have a bank, where is it located and what is the current balance? 5. The last budget report to membership 6. Please list any Political Action Committees associated with the chapter. Do they have bank accounts? What are their balances? 7. Any disciplinary notices from state or city agencies within the last year. 8. Chapter email, address, and socials 9. The current bylaws of the chapter 10. The current roster of officers 11. The date of your last annual meeting / convention? 2. Two (2) Year Grace Period. Chapters have up to two years after convention to apply for a new charter. Failure to do so may mean the chapter is not in compliance and appropriate action will be taken as outlined here. 1. The NPC, or a delegated body will produce an omnibus approval block of charter renewals 2. The NPC, or a delegated body will have the power to pull individual charters that are deemed problematic to be voted on individually by the NPC-SC Section 7. Enforcement of Charter 1. Request for investigation and appeal: The National Political Committee can place in trusteeship (meaning direct administration) any Chapter found to be in violation of chapter agreement, for a period of 3, 6, or 12 months, based on the severity and duration of the violation. No Chapter may be placed in trusteeship except by vote of ⅔ of the entire membership of the NPC. The Steering Committee of the National Political Committee, or a delegate chosen for the purpose by the SC, may investigate Chapters suspected of non-compliance with the national Constitution and Bylaws, Chapter Agreements, or both. A report detailing the suspected non-compliance shall be provided to the SC and the Co-Chairs of the Chapter in question, with specific reference to the rules or provisions being violated and the date(s), nature and extent of the violations. The Chapter may provide a written response to the report no more than twenty-eight days after receipt of the report. If the SC, after the twenty-eight day response period, by majority vote finds that the Chapter is not in compliance, the Steering Committee may withhold dues from that Chapter. Should the Chapter not remediate the violation(s) within ninety days, the Steering Committee may by simple majority vote deny the Chapter access to organization-wide tools and data. Any decision imposing penalties on a Chapter must be communicated in writing to the Chapter’s Co-Chairs and members within five days of its adoption. A Chapter may, by written request of any of its elected officers or by petition of five (5) percent of its members, appeal any imposed penalty to the full NPC which may by simple majority of a quorate vote confirm, reduce, or repeal the penalty(ies). Such appeal must be heard and acted upon in no more than forty days, but no less than ten days, of receipt by the NPC. 2. Notice of Violation. DSA, through the NPC, shall be responsible for enforcing this Agreement and shall provide written Notice of Violations of this Agreement to CHAPTER with a minimum of (28) days to correct any breach of the Agreement. In the event that CHAPTER fails to correct any breach of the Agreement or to respond within the time period specified within the Notice, DSA through the NPC, may withhold resources to the chapter. If the breach of charter is still not correct after these actions, then the NPC may revoke CHAPTER’s Charter or establish Trusteeship over the Charter pursuant to the procedures specified in this Agreement. 3. Withholding resources. DSA, through the NPC, shall have the authority to limit or completely withhold the dues share or suspend the chapter’s access to Org Tools. 4. Trusteeship. DSA, through the NPC, shall have the authority to establish Trusteeship of CHAPTER if CHAPTER fails to comply with or respond to any Notice of Violation of this Agreement within the specified time period or in the event that half or more of the elected leadership of a chapter resigns. In the event that Trusteeship is established, the NPC or its designees shall act as Officers of CHAPTER until such time as new Officers may be democratically elected by the Membership but for a period no longer than 1 year. 5. Revocation of Charter. DSA, through the NPC, shall have the authority to revoke the charter of CHAPTER if CHAPTER fails to comply with or respond to any Notice of Violation of this Agreement within the specified time period. 6. Termination of Charter. CHAPTER may terminate this CHARTER and affiliation with DSA at any time. CHAPTER may initiate Termination of Charter through written notice of its intention to do so no less than thirty (30) days prior to the effective date of such termination. DSA reserves the right to all assets bearing DSA’s name and/or insignia and may request that they be surrendered by CHAPTER on the date of termination, including but not limited to email addresses, website domains, social media accounts, and publications. Capacity Commitment & Financial Impact Scores[6] Capacity 3: Moderate to High Finances 1: Less than $5000 The recommendation introduces a robust new compliance framework (chapter affiliation agreements) that requires substantial coordination from both staff and NPC members. Implementation involves training chapters on new requirements, conducting investigations, managing appeals, and overseeing enforcement actions such as dues withholding or access restrictions to organizational tools. Moving to a proactive trusteeship model represents a major increase in workload beyond current operations. Staff will need to support legal review, documentation, communications, and compliance monitoring, especially if multiple chapters require intervention. Financial Impact is scored a 2 due to expected administrative costs such as document formatting, internal communications, compliance tracking systems, and potential legal advice requirements. While most activities rely on existing infrastructure and personnel, there may be moderate expenses related to training materials, platform adjustments, and increased tech or legal support needs. There are no major infrastructure investments or external contracts required, keeping costs within a manageable range despite the high time demand. Status: Adopted Summary Given the declining state of US-led world imperialism, return of US expansionist policy, and DSA being the largest Socialist organization within the US, DSA IC has requested to continue being a Priority Committee, designating both Progressive International as our political international and all invited international observers to National Convention 2025 as DSA’s Priority International Partners, and expanding DSA’s national capacity to campaign against U.S. empire and for International solidarity. Full text WHEREAS, an international coalition of ruling class oligarchies led by the United States increasingly threaten the sovereignty of democratically elected governments and international structures. WHEREAS, the Trump administration is reverting to the most belligerent forms of U.S. imperialism, including direct threats of conquest and imposition of widespread tariffs as a weapon of global economic warfare, creates further urgency to expand DSA’s internationalist organizing. WHEREAS, DSA being the largest socialist organization within the United States is increasingly asked by socialist parties and movements in other countries for analyses of what is happening in the USA and for reciprocal solidarity against U.S. imperialist interventions. WHEREAS, over the past 8 years, DSA has engaged in a variety of international solidarity efforts including organizing against the Cuban Embargo, BDS and Palestine solidarity campaigns, and immigrant justice organizing. WHEREAS, since its reform in 2019, DSA IC has developed a broad swath of international diplomatic relations with parties abroad, particularly in Latin America through its membership in the São Paulo Forum since 2022. WHEREAS, over the last two years the U.S.-Israeli genocide of the Palestinian people has led to a significant transformation of the American Left with an increased internationalist character. Therefore, let it be resolved, DSA shall continue to designate the International Committee (IC) as the Priority Committee of the organization responsible for coordination of DSA’s diplomatic relations and reciprocal exchange programs with all organizations abroad, as well as international solidarity and anti-imperialist campaign work inside the United States. Be it further resolved, DSA shall designate the Progressive International (PI) as the “Political International” it is a member of and will regularly participate in strategic PI activities including delegations, educational efforts, and joint campaigns. Be it further resolved, DSA shall coordinate with PI a speaking tour across DSA chapters featuring progressive party leaders, parliamentarians, labor activists, and social movement activists by the 2027 DSA Convention. Be it further resolved, DSA shall designate the international parties and other organizations invited to observe this convention as “Priority International Partners” for DSA as coordinated by the appropriate divisions of the International Committee. Be it further resolved, DSA International Committee shall be responsible for building deep solidaristic bonds with Priority International Partners through joint political education projects and classes and joint campaigns. DSA IC will also strive to expand relationships with PIPs beyond the IC through the facilitation of meetings and programming with DSA National Committee leaders and chapter leaders. Be it further resolved, the DSA International Committee will be responsible for maintaining an updated list of Priority International Partners with a priority on organizations from the Global South. Be it further resolved, DSA IC recognizes that it has not successfully developed the chapter liaisons program, or strategic campaigns enough to coordinate a powerful national anti-imperialist campaigning apparatus that meets the current moment. Be it further resolved, DSA IC commits to launching two official priority campaigns by the end of 2025 focused on Immigrant justice and Palestine Solidarity. Be it further resolved, DSA chapters are encouraged to merge existing internationalist, anti-war, immigrant justice, and Palestine solidarity committees into unified chapter International Committees. If such a consolidation is not possible, then DSA chapters are encouraged to have a chapter liaison from each body responsible for internationalist work. Be it further resolved, DSA International Committee will experiment with various mechanisms to integrate chapter International Committees such as regular convenings of chapter IC leaders, expedited member onboarding for chapter IC members, and training series on how to build chapter level internationalism. Be it further resolved, DSA encourages At-Large members residing outside of the USA to engage with socialist organizations in their country of residence. DSA IC will track and develop these relationships through diplomatic support. Be it further resolved, DSA IC shall develop a regular bulletin compiling updates about the International left, DSA internationalist organizing, and U.S. empire. Be it further resolved, DSA IC will facilitate the creation of internationalist merchandise for the DSA store. Cost Estimate National Speaking tour: $2,000 One year of Immigrant Justice and Palestine solidarity priority campaigns: $4,000 Total: $6,000 Capacity Commitment & Financial Impact Scores Capacity 1: Minimal Finances 2: $5000 to $10,000 This resolution received a Capacity Commitment score of 1 due to the fact that much of the work described builds upon its ongoing efforts within the IC. While there is some expansion in scope, the expectations fall within manageable limits for current staff involvement and members. It received a Financial Impact score of 2 , reflecting limited direct costs of $6,000 for key activities, with no indication of significant additional expenses beyond current capacity. Status: Rejected Summary DSA should build relationships with a diverse array of left parties and movements in other countries, including those in and out of government. DSA should learn from and stand in solidarity with movements in the Global South fighting for democracy and socialism against all governments that engage in the repression of democratic rights and side with capital over workers. Finally, DSA should re-affirm that the NPC is the highest decision-making body of the organization between Conventions. Full text Whereas, 1. Internationalism is a core principle of democratic socialist politics. Capitalism is a global system that exploits and oppresses workers across the world to enrich a small capitalist minority in the Global North. The international working class transcends borders and must be united in its fight against exploitation and oppression and to replace capitalism with democratic socialism. Socialists stand in solidarity with workers and popular movements around the world in their struggle for socialism and democracy, and a world free from exploitation and oppression. 2. The emancipation of the working class must be undertaken by the working class itself. Only the self-activity of workers can end capitalism and realize socialism. As such, socialists must support democracy and rank-and-file control within working-class organizations, trade unions and political parties. Only through a clear-eyed commitment to expansive political democracy and freedoms can democratic socialism be achieved and maintained. We must remain cognizant of the pressures of imperialism and the circumstances of socialist movements across the world and not dictate to mass socialist movements, but we also must not waver in our democratic principles. 3. Over the past few years, DSA's international work has advanced and developed significantly, while at the same time, DSA's international work has been at times out of step with our membership and broader strategy. DSA should continue to oppose cynical attempts of the US and other western powers to undermine political figures and nations that do not fall in line with their imperial interests. The failure of western governments to stand up against the genocide in Gaza highlights how opposition to un-aligned countries and political movements are highly selective and motivated by ruling class interests, rather than any genuine commitment to human rights and international law. 4. However, while remaining unwavering in our opposition to imperial interference, DSA’s international work should not reflexively and uncritically celebrate any such political figures and nations simply because of their opposition to United States imperialism. Our commitments to democratic socialist principles and nuanced political analysis cannot end at our own borders. Instead, DSA's international work should assess political figures and nations critically from the perspective of the interests of the international working class, and embrace the breadth and diversity of working class social movements, political formations, and labor unions around the world by making connections to a wide variety of working class organizations on the ground fighting for socialism and democracy across the globe, not just those with government-sanctioned power. Arming our working class base with an accurate balance sheet of the successes and shortcomings of international figures, movements, and governments can help build a broad and effective mass resistance to global imperialism in the United States, which is among our most crucial tasks. 5. Furthermore, as a US-based organization our role is not to judge foreign political movements – whether to praise or denounce them - but to analyze their conditions and how we relate to them. Our international commentary must be laser focused on exposing, critiquing, and dismantling imperialism originating from the US and its allies. Be it further resolved, DSA will take a “big-tent” approach to building relationships with socialist movements, groups, organizations, and parties in other countries. This means meeting and building relationships with a diverse array of left parties and movements in other countries. This includes those in and out of government, as well as independent workers’ organizations and trade unions.

Be it further resolved, DSA recognizes and reaffirms our duty to learn from and stand in solidarity with movements in the Global South and around the world that are fighting for democracy and socialism against all governments that engage in the repression of democratic rights and side with capital over workers. This necessarily includes governments that ally with U.S. empire and governments that claim to oppose U.S. imperialism, but which continue to repress or exploit their own working class populations. By "democracy," we mean democratic rights including the rights to: * independently form and organize trade unions and political organizations; * to vote in meaningful political processes that choose government leaders; * free speech and expression, including the right to criticize and protest one's own government; * equality for all racial and ethnic groups, gender identities and expressions, and sexualities; * indigenous and national self-determination;

Be it further resolved, our main targets are our own government and the global structure of exploitation and imperialism that it maintains. However, as consistent anti-imperialists and internationalists, our starting point for establishing solidarity must be the rights of workers and peoples, not the balance of geopolitical power or the nominal political identities of different governments. Be it further resolved, DSA opposes imperialist interventions that claim to support democracy or workers’ movements through broad economic sanctions and military intervention, intelligence operations, or state funding of opposition groups. We oppose all measures that act as collective punishment against a country’s population, harm workers, and deny national sovereignty. Anti-democratic, imperialist interventions by the United States and other capitalist countries undermine and delegitimize grassroots movements for democracy by associating them with foreign intervention, thereby providing cover for governments to suppress democracy in the name of anti-imperialism and national sovereignty. Principled criticisms of governments and policies that restrict democracy or attack the working class does equate to support for imperialist intervention or regime change, just as criticism of liberal or progressive politicians domestically does not imply support for their reactionary and conservative opponents. Be it further resolved, DSA re-affirms that the National Political Committee, being the democratically elected leadership of our organization, is the highest decision-making body of the organization between meetings of the Convention. DSA re-affirms that the NPC has the authority to exert political oversight over the IC, and make final determinations about any statements or policy positions developed by the IC. ________________ Capacity Commitment & Financial Impact Scores Capacity 1: Minimal Finances 1: Less than $5000 This amendment does not affect the overall capacity or cost requirements for the underlying resolution. Status: Adopted Summary This resolution outlines NPEC’s intent to meet urgent demands on DSA to lead politically as a pre-party organization, by increasing its resources and capacity to better serve DSA members and the wider public. This is so crucial now, as we see educators and learners under attack, as liberal institutions fail their missions to defend free expression and knowledge and collaborate with the right. Socialists must answer fascistic repression with socialist humanism. Full text Whereas: NPEC was founded in 2019, with a mission to “invest”–organize and expand–political education within DSA to contribute to the development of our members as socialist organizers and more broadly, as promoters of and participants in democracy; NPEC has met and surpassed its ambit of work originally described in 2019, with the development of socialist night schools, a podcast, a newsletter, core trainings and curricula, and regular events; offshoots like Archives Workshops and the Capital Reading Group; and successful cross-collaborations with DSA committees and groups outside DSA, like the We Are the Union reading group with DSA Labor and EWOC; Now, in the wake of huge political upheaval and membership surges, NPEC has found ourselves meeting more need than ever within DSA, as thousands of new socialists have come to us in search of meaningful political belonging, learning, and direction; NPEC punches far above our weight given limited resources, due to the high level of dedication of our members, but administrative tasks constrain our capacity, and we could use more material support from the national organization to continue building the large, dynamic educative apparatus that befits DSA as a pre-party formation; Education–the teachers, faculty, students, researchers, librarians, all workers who make learning and knowledge available to humanity–in the US is under heavy fire, from outside the school gates and from inside. Institutions touted as guardians of free expression and claimed as bulwarks of democracy attack their own students and censor their teachers as education, ever more costly, is turned into mere credentialism; So-called “woke” and “Marxist” knowledge production and preservation have been the primary targets of the right, which brings within its scope of attack courses and materials about capitalism, climate change, racism, queerness, feminism, imperialism, social movements, and class struggle; To meet this watershed moment, socialists must once again take up their traditional role as vigorous defenders of education, and build DSA to stand as a pillar of socialist humanism–the idea that knowledge is a social good, it must be universally available, and it must be directed to diverse human flourishing, and the collective uplift and freedom of the working class; NPEC must be re-invested now so DSA can fully contribute to the crucial and expansive fight against fascistic censorship and authoritarian repression, by promoting pro-social knowledge production that defends education and strengthens our own organization as an institution of knowledge flow and production in its own right. Resolved: NPEC WILL INCREASE OUR CAPACITY: NPEC continues its commitment to building a diverse, multi-tendency committee that can meet our urgent political moment, and expand our capacity. In addition to energetic outreach to all parts of our organization for recruitment to the main committee each application term, NPEC will revitalize our “Volunteers and Contributors” program for temporary and short-term work with NPEC by: * advertising V&C more frequently; * engaging in direct asks of national and chapter leadership and political educators to recruit and recommend members to NPEC; * creating more opportunities for shorter-term support projects to build skills across DSA and increase poli-ed cadre and capacity on the national and local levels. Depending on an assessment of our successes and needs in this area by December 2025, V&C may become its own subcommittee by vote of NPEC. NPEC WILL INCREASE OUR RESOURCES: Resource commitments to the National Political Education Committee and its projects will increase in the following two ways: * Dedicated staff time, equivalent to up to 10 hours per week, to aid the steering committee and our rank and file members execute publication and distribution of our materials, archiving and web work, basic communications, scheduling, and other administrative tasks. * A political education allocation in the DSA budget of $20,000 in 2026 for materials and honoraria for events, technical equipment/software, reading group subsidies, reward swag, and other material investments to promote and expand DSA’s political education, with an increase of up to 50% for 2027’s budget, contingent on the previous year’s spending and impact assessments, in consultation with relevant DSA committees, leadership and national staff. NPEC WILL INCREASE OUR OUTREACH: The committee will continue to build on its successes in outreach, including the following increases: * The expansion and diversification of the Class podcast in content, frequency, personnel, and reach, with the goal of weekly podcasts by December 2025; * Improving the poli-ed reach of DSA’s YouTube channel with the support of DSA’s communications department, with a goal of increasing views of NPEC’s new video content double by December 2025; * Increased collaboration and crossover with other DSA committees to support those committees’ campaign or internal work with pedagogical and training support, and to create new avenues for poli-ed within DSA and outside of it, with a goal of three new crossover events or curricular projects by December 2025, six by December 2026, and three by August 2027; * Where NPEC presently hosts a yearly Educators’ Conference, three additional quarterly gatherings shall be organized to improve our connection with and foster collaboration between local chapters’ political education programs. NPEC WILL INCREASE OUR CURRICULA: NPEC commits to making an even larger and more dynamic set of curricula that strengthens our members’ intellectual muscles at every level and creates opportunities to build debate, critique and engagement skills that learners can take into their chapters, unions, and community organizing spaces. These curricula will be available to members via NPEC’s Moodle as they are created and as fully as possible. * The committee will assess current materials and resources and from that basis, create four new Socialist Night School series of 3-4 parts each, on the following topics, seeking the support and collaboration of the NPC and relevant committees, to be completed within one year of 2025 convention (ie, by August 2026), rolled out one per quarter, and advertised widely. After these SNSes are completed and used, they will be assessed, and a new program for four new SNS series will be proposed and executed by NPEC between August 2026-7. The first four shall be on the following topics: * Democracy, Civil Society, and Socialist Politics * What is Internationalism for Socialists? * Socialist Analyses of Nativism and Racism * Socialist Feminisms & Gender Liberation * The committee will partner with local chapters’ political education programs to compile informative content made by DSA members nationwide. The committee will select, review, and edit these materials where appropriate to prepare them for national distribution. * The committee will create a Party School program that will complement leadership training within the Growth and Development Committee. * The committee will create a basic Socialist Sprouts Curricula for parents, caregivers, and children. * The committee will run the Capital Reading Group at least once per year. * The committee will host other reading groups as proposed and approved as frequently as capacity allows, and will create channels for interested groups of members who wish to activate a reading group to petition for support and resources from NPEC, to encourage and expand reading capacity and skills in DSA and across the working class. Status: Adopted, as amended Summary This resolution was democratically decided on by the membership of DSA’s national Electoral Commission. It contains proposals for running candidates as independents, changing our endorsement criteria, and Socialists in Office Committees. Full text Whereas: After the 2023 convention, DSA’s National Electoral Commission became an open commission whose job is to lead DSA’s national electoral work and to carry out electoral related DSA convention resolutions. Any DSA member in good standing with electoral experience is eligible to be an NEC member. Whereas: While the NEC Steering Committee recommends national endorsements, leads sub-committees and implements NEC projects, the commission is governed by its membership, who democratically determine the leadership, structure, and political direction of the NEC. Whereas: In this term, the NEC SC has recommended multiple candidates for national endorsement, launched a fundraising campaign for nationally endorsed candidates, raising over 25 thousand dollars, and provided training materials, education, and mentorship to chapters across the organization. Whereas: The below resolved clauses were democratically written, debated, amended and approved by the NEC at-large membership. They are representative of the multi-tendency nature of this body and lay out a democratic vision for DSA’s electoral work for the next two years. Whereas: * DSA chapters across the country have had increasing successes in drafting DSA leaders and activists to run for down ballot office as “cadre” candidates, where campaigns communications and operations are closely intertwined with local chapter organizing. While political conditions vary heavily across the country, down ballot races for state and local office are often winnable for local chapters given our movement’s current scale and resources. * The Democratic Party faces an unprecedented crisis of disapproval and distrust among working-class voters across the country, creating new openings for insurgent socialist challengers and oppositional politics. DSA could seize our unique moment by making strategic investments in local party-building to challenge the political establishment at the grassroots level. * DSA has encountered debate and controversy with questions of candidate accountability when endorsing candidates who go on to take positions or actions which are out of alignment with DSA’s platform or priorities. Investing in running more cadre candidates would ensure that going forward, DSA is running more candidates who are in strong political alignment with our organization’s political perspective, and who will stay closely connected to local chapters as well as the national organization. * Over the past year, the NEC launched a nationwide fundraising push “Socialist Cash Takes Out Capitalist Trash!” which raised tens of thousands of dollars to support nationally-endorsed DSA candidates running for state and local office around the country. The success of this initiative proves what DSA can accomplish when acting like a party: together, we can make interventions in local elections which are politically coherent, materially impactful, democratically organized and member-led. * To move towards developing a real working-class political party, DSA must reject an NGO-aligned, top-down or service model of staffing, towards a politicized and bottom-up model where member-leaders are empowered to take on political work in full-time positions to share lessons and skills with fellow members across the country and work directly with local chapters to plan their campaigns. Section 1: Recruitment of Independent and Nonpartisan Candidates Resolved: The NEC will form a subcommittee to recruit at least three socialists to run as independent or nonpartisan candidates in 2026-2028 local, state, or federal elections. These candidates will be considered for national endorsement by the NEC and NPC and only run if they are endorsed by the national organization. This subcommittee, the “Independent and Nonpartisan Candidates Subcommittee” will be composed of 2 NPC members selected by the body and 4 NEC members selected by the NEC and approved by the NPC. Within one month of the national convention they will present a timeline and work plan to the NPC for approval and select a committee chair to helm organizational work. The role of this subcommittee will be to: * Identify strategic districts where a socialist candidate would be popular, and the race is non-partisan or advantageous for independent candidates. They should use factors such as * The strength and interest of the local DSA chapters and use factors such as: * Willingness to run an independent campaign * Experience being the primary organization running previous campaigns * A large number of members with experience canvassing, fundraising, handling communications, compliance, volunteer recruitment and staff positions * Have the ability to set up an SIO committee * Past election results of previous socialist candidates including Bernie Sanders and voter registration statistics. * A district and constituency analysis and power mapping such as, but not limited to, median income, active labor unions with DSA member involvement, university student presence or active YDSA chapter, and number of tenants * Compliance and legal requirements * Work with chapter leaders and national committees to identify and recruit cadre DSA members to run for office as independents. They should use factors such as * A demonstrated commitment to DSA through being an active leader and regularly participating in DSA events and debates * A commitment to building a socialist slate and political independence. * A history of activity and leadership in their unions, social movements and local communities * Willingness and ability to run an effective campaign and do tasks such as knock on thousands of doors, participate in debates, speak publicly and other routine campaign activities * Research the compliance and legal requirements of running as independents All candidates who run on the socialist slate as independents must agree to the following: * Run only as an independents * Agree to run on a slate with all other nationally endorsed independent candidates and participate in the joint fundraising program * Prominently feature the term “democratic socialist” and discuss DSA on their literature, social media and in speeches * Agree to participate in the Socialists in Office Committee of the local chapter while campaigning and if elected * Agree with and campaign on our nationally agreed-on policy platform These candidates will receive the following support from DSA, coordinated by the committee and executed by the NEC. * A robust fundraising campaign * National phone banks coordinated by the NEC * Being prominently featured in DSA communications and social media * The NPC will work with the NEC to create a “Independent and Nonpartisan Candidates Subcommittee” to coordinate these efforts * Other efforts organized by the Committee After the conclusion of the campaign, the committee will conduct debriefs with the campaigns and compile the findings into strategy advice for future campaigns. Section 2: Focused National Endorsements Resolved: The criteria for National DSA Endorsements will be redefined so that national DSA endorsements should be strategically focused on electoral campaigns where DSA intends to make concerted national action to intervene in elections. These endorsement criteria may result in fewer endorsements, but will allow for more meaningful endorsements. The criteria for national endorsement applications will ask that candidates: * Have a demonstrated history of leadership in their chapter, participation in DSA’s internal life, and attending DSA events. * Commit to uphold DSA’s national policy platform, Workers Deserve More, and DSA’s national priorities, campaigns and initiatives * View themselves as socialist organizers first, and legislators second * Openly and proudly identify with DSA and Socialism, including by: * Expressly encouraging people to join DSA * Identifying publicly as a “Socialist” or “Democratic Socialist,” * Aligning their branding, messaging, and/or color scheme with DSA. * Commit to grow their DSA chapter and develop DSA leaders through their campaign * Demonstrate interest in receiving a national endorsement * Commit to caucusing with fellow elected DSA endorsees and socialist-in-office committees, where applicable National endorsements should also consider: * How DSA’s national endorsement would significantly impact the odds of success, through national fundraising, publicity, and volunteer support. * Opportunities to build DSA’s public profile and recruit more members through elections with national political significance. * The campaign’s stance on key political issues and strategic questions important to DSA, such as: * The Democratic Party, political independence and party-building * DSA’s path to power and the transition to a socialist society * Palestinian liberation National endorsements for federal candidates require the following additional criteria: * Elected leadership of the chapter(s) requesting endorsement must meet with the NPC to discuss the chapter’s role in the campaign, how the candidate aligns with the chapter’s political and strategic priorities, how the chapter will support the campaign operationally, and how national DSA and the chapter will coordinate around the campaign. This requirement is not applicable for presidential candidates. * Candidates must meet with the NPC to discuss their questionnaires and stances on key political and strategic questions important to DSA. This meeting is observable by any NEC member in good standing. NPC may extend the meeting under executive session at their own discretion. * After the endorsement meeting(s) with the NPC, an endorsement recommendation to the NPC will be debated and voted on by NEC rank and file members at an NEC all-member meeting, observable by any DSA member in good standing. * The NPC will hold at least one open membership discussion event regarding the candidate's endorsement, open to all DSA members in good standing. * NPC votes on federal candidate endorsements will take place only in synchronous NPC meetings, observable by any DSA member in good standing. NPC’s meetings with chapters and candidates may not be combined, the candidate must meet with the NPC individually. NEC SC members may attend and participate in both meetings. NEC’s Endorsements Subcommittee must prepare summaries of both meetings available to NEC members in good standing prior to NEC’s recommendation vote. In line with DSA's existing national endorsement practices, NEC recommendations are non-binding. And whereas, DSA’s national endorsement is a key tool for developing a party-like identity and political practice for DSA, a goal which was affirmed in Consensus Resolution Amendment 6-1, “Act Like an Independent Party,” at the 2023 DSA Convention..

And whereas, candidates who receive the DSA national endorsement are broadly taken to be representative of DSA’s politics.

And whereas, although DSA encompasses a wide range of political positions, there are basic standards of political conduct which are broadly intuitive to DSA members, the violation of which by endorsed candidates has caused significant internal conflict in the past.

Full text Whereas, DSA has repeatedly affirmed our commitment to housing justice and the mission of the Housing Justice Commission in 2021 and 2023 through R21 and CR 1 respectively, Whereas, DSA has adopted “The 4 Principles of Social Housing” as our organizational definition of social housing and recognizes that only the replacement of the private housing market with social housing can achieve housing justice, Whereas, DSA recognizes the creation of an organized, nationwide movement of militant tenant unionists as the prerequisite for achieving social housing so defined, Whereas, The tenant movement across the United States has grown rapidly in strength and is increasingly conscious of its place at the leading edge of the class struggle; Whereas, the tenant movement remains geographically fragmented and has yet to coalesce around a national program or plan of action; Whereas, DSA chapters across the country generally do not yet promote the formation of new socialist tenant unions capable of running themselves and growing our base for social housing; DSA categorically rejects so-called “market-based solutions” to the housing crisis that reify the ownership of land and shelter by landlords and private developers. Universally accessible

Be it resolved, DSA affirms that the purpose of our tenant organizing activities is to create and strengthen tenant unions led democratically by rank-and-file tenants and not NGOs. Be it resolved, the HJC will work with chapters to create draft resolutions setting disclosure standards around tenant organizing work. These resolutions will set expectations around disclosing when a member is a landlord, works in real estate, or holds leadership roles in housing-related nonprofits when engaging in work or running for leadership in housing-related bodies. Be it resolved, DSA recognizes the importance of language justice within the tenant movement by encouraging members to learn Spanish and other languages through the expansion of the HJC’s language exchange project. As a part of onboarding new members into DSA, DSA will ask members what languages they speak and the next membership survey will include a question on what languages members speak. The list of members who speak languages included in the language exchange project will be shared with the project leadership. Be it resolved, DSA reauthorizes the Housing Justice Commission as a priority commission until 2027. Be it resolved, HJC will create a nationwide “Socialists: Organize your workplace, Organize your Building” campaign that will educate DSA members on the importance of organizing both at work and at home. Be it resolved, DSA will increase HJC’s capacity to support tenant organizing projects in all DSA chapters by: * Completing a mapping assessment of tenant organizing capacity in DSA including * Finding current chapters with tenant organizing working groups or projects specifically dedicated to organizing and supporting existing and new Tenant Associations and Tenant Unions * Asking new members what tenant union they are a members of during the join process * Asking members what tenant union they are a members of as part of any membership survey * Sharing this information with the HJC who will connect members to ETOC and/or existing chapter-based tenant organizing projects like NYC-DSA’s Independent Working Class Organizing initiative (IWCO) * Supporting outreach to chapters to gauge their interest in creating a tenant organizing project or working group.
