Status: Referred to NPC Summary This resolution sets DSA on a course to build a socialist party through constructing and strengthening local pre-party formations, developing the left wing of the labor movement, launching a socialist slate of candidates, and bringing together aligned organizations in shared struggle. Full text Whereas, the Trump administration is escalating the war on the working class via attacks on abortion rights and trans rights, the rising costs of living, mass deportations, expansions of global imperialism, and crackdowns on the labor movement. Whereas, the Democratic Party has utterly failed to counter the threat of Trump over the past decade, failed to address working people’s economic concerns or protect abortion rights during the Biden Administration, and ran a disastrous Harris/Walz campaign which led to Trump’s return to office. Whereas, the strategy of the socialist left supporting the Democratic Party as a safeguard for working people against Trump and the right wing Republican Party or quietly attaching ourselves to them is a losing one, as association with the Democratic Party political brand handicaps the horizons of our movement, which endeavors to overthrow the capitalist system that both capitalist parties exist to protect. Whereas, the Democratic Party and its representatives are at historically low levels of approval, and Trump’s dangerous policies are alienating millions of workers. Whereas, DSA has a critical role to play in winning the support of workers away from the Democratic and Republican parties by proving that socialism addresses the material needs of the working class and poses a much stronger challenge to the right wing than liberalism can. Whereas, the logical progression of DSA’s political work points towards the establishment of a mass socialist political party rooted in the struggles of the working class and oppressed people that poses a challenge to the capitalist class on all fronts. We as DSA and as socialists are the conscious layer of the working class, and so we have a responsibility to use our conscious effort to accelerate the process of developing the party, rather than expecting its genesis to emerge gradually. Whereas, a socialist party will develop at different rates and will take on different forms depending on state and local contexts, and a national strategy is needed to coordinate across and link these developments together. Therefore be it resolved that DSA commits to establishing a socialist party by or before the end of the Trump Presidency, and embarks on a conscious party-building project. This socialist party will be a democratically run political organization that takes on the following projects. * Waging class struggle against the Trump administration and capitalist forces, including capitalist political parties, corporate interests, and the military industrial complex through sustained campaigns, rallies, protests, rank and file organizing, political education, and direct action. * Coordinating mass movements, rank and file labor organizing, and electoral campaigns and linking them under a socialist banner and theory of change. * Running electoral campaigns at federal, state, and local levels with a common socialist brand and program, connecting across a myriad of local socialist and left wing de facto and official party formations, slates, and caucuses. * Developing socialist and working-class democratic institutions at national and local levels to combat and supplant the hegemony of capitalist civil institutions, including local business alliances, developer and landlord interests, the capitalist police, and bourgeois media. Resolved, that throughout the Trump Presidency, DSA will continue to take a leading role in the struggle against Trump and the right wing through bold campaigns that fight for improvements in workers’ material conditions and highlight the failure of the Democratic Party to oppose Trump and fight for working people. The NPC will prioritize its role as political leadership of DSA and coordinate rapid response to developing struggles, including nationwide days of action, mass calls, panels and debates, and coordination with staff, chapters, and committees. Resolved, that DSA aims to win over critical layers of the labor movement to support a socialist party. To do so, the NLC will coordinate DSA members within their unions to strengthen existing reform caucuses and build new ones as needed. Simultaneously, the NLC will pursue building the socialist and left wing of those reform caucuses and the labor movement as a whole. We aim to orient the labor movement towards a socialist perspective via active recruitment, resolutions at the local and national level, and diligent shop-floor work. Resolved, that DSA’s party-building project will take on the following general timeline. * Following convention, the NPC will identify a list of key unions, reform caucuses, workers organizations, and other left-wing and progressive groups that we may be able to work alongside to build a socialist party, on the basis of factors including political alignment with DSA, history of joint campaigns and shared struggle with DSA, and the development of DSA’s rank-and-file presence in the organization. The NPC will conduct or delegate outreach to these groups to assess alignment on party-building, to organize together on shared campaigns, and to make asks for endorsement of our socialist slate and participation in our launch conference. * Following convention, the NPC and NEC will conduct systematic outreach and work with all DSA chapters to outline plans for the establishment of de facto or official municipal or statewide parties. These formations may consist of a socialist caucus of endorsed electeds, outward messaging and branding, or a ballot line under which some or all endorsed electeds run. In order to develop candidates from DSA’s ranks and strengthen chapter-level electoral programs for our socialist slate and beyond, the NEC will develop a nationally planned electoral training program modeled on Louisville DSA’s electoral academy with the goal of launching it in at least 20 chapters by the end of 2026. * DSA will endorse and run a socialist slate of candidates for the 2026 elections. The slate will feature at least 10 candidates (including at least 4 congressional candidates) who are endorsed by the NPC and by their local chapters. DSA will adopt a shared branding for the campaigns and will highlight the slate as showing how a socialist party would operate as DSA seeks to build one. The candidates on the slate will meet the following baseline expectations. * Publicly and prominently refer to themselves as “socialists” or “democratic socialists” rather than “Democrat” or “progressive” throughout all aspects of their campaign, regardless of their ballot line. * Forming a socialist caucus with all other DSA endorsed officials in the same legislative body, running on local or statewide slates with all DSA endorsed candidates in the same chapter or legislative body, and participating in national and chapter-level Socialist in Office Committees. * Adopting and promoting all programs, and policies agreed upon by the NPC, NEC, and/or their local DSA chapter. * Publicly describing themselves as a DSA member, consistently calling on their supporters and constituents to join DSA, and highlighting their part in the launch of a new socialist party. * By the end of the Trump term, DSA and all of the organizations we have won over to our party-building project will hold a launch conference, where we will discuss questions of political strategy, coordination across a myriad of different state and local party formations, our plans for the 2028 elections, and structure, democracy and leadership in the party. This resolution turns our ad hoc Trump response into a focused national campaign, with resources and a clear mission needed to fight the right. Full Text Whereas, 1. Donald Trump has returned to the White House, leading an administration that poses a direct and unprecedented threat to whatever semblance of democracy the United States has, including workers’ rights, immigrants, LGBTQ+ people (in particular trans people), women, and all oppressed communities. His administration has escalated attacks on civil liberties, intensified state repression (in particular of Palestinian rights organizers), and emboldened far-right forces across the country. 2. The Trump administration is undertaking a full-scale privatization of federal institutions, gutting labor protections, environmental regulations, and public services while stacking agencies with reactionary loyalists. This represents not only a power grab by the far right but a wholesale effort by segments of capital to privatize the state and roll back the meagre rights clawed out by generations of militant workers’ struggle. 3. The Democratic Party has failed to stop the rise of the far right and is actively shifting rightward in response. Democrats have repeatedly capitulated to reactionary policies, abandoned workers, and allowed the erosion of democratic institutions. Even in power, they have prioritized protecting capitalist stability over fighting the right, leaving working people with little meaningful opposition or opportunities to engage with formal politics. 4. The failures of the Democratic Party have allowed the far right to begin to capture large segments of the working class. After decades of broken promises, neoliberal policies, and indifference to the material suffering of workers, many—including workers of color and young people—have disengaged or defected to reactionary forces. Only an organized, independent socialist movement can provide a real alternative. 5. Despite the extreme threat posed by the Trump administration and the far right, the Democratic Party remains a primary political opponent of the working class in the Democratic controlled states, cities, and districts where DSA is often strongest. Fighting the far right means resisting capitulation by Democratic leadership in these areas, winning back working class people (particularly young people and people of color) in Democratic strongholds who have flipped to Trump or fallen out of participating in politics entirely, and ultimately winning local level socialist governance in our strongest areas. 6. The Trump administration’s attacks on the labor movement and the federal workforce represent a key battleground for resistance. His administration seeks to dismantle the National Labor Relations Board (NLRB), impose a national right-to-work law, purge public-sector unions, eradicate the civil service, and eviscerate worker protections. This is a direct assault on the working class of this country. 7. DSA must position itself as the leading force against the Trump administration and the far right by organizing mass resistance, building a working-class movement that can mobilize at every level, and seizing this moment to recruit tens of thousands of new members. 8. DSA is uniquely positioned to recruit thousands of new dues-paying members and should invest additional financial and volunteer resources to recruit and run hundreds of new socialist candidates to replace weak, complicit Democrats at all levels of government across the country. DSA must also build more national capacity to support and grow chapter campaigns for electoral office, ballot measures, legislation, and other tactics that can build a force that can oppose right-wing power at the grassroots level. 9. Defeating the far right requires more than just fighting back—it requires building the Left. DSA must use this moment to massively grow our ranks, train new leaders, and build organizational infrastructure capable of sustaining a long-term struggle for socialism. 10. Defending our members against state repression and far-right violence is not optional—it is necessary for survival. DSA must equip chapters with the tools to protect members, develop security protocols, and prepare for the likelihood of state crackdowns on labor organizing, protest movements, and socialist organizations. DSA must prepare our organization’s own legal protection and do all we can to protect our members, in particular trans, migrant, and Palestinian members. 11. Socialists cannot rely primarily on existing institutions to resist authoritarianism. NGOs, Democratic-aligned advocacy groups, and progressive organizations have consistently failed to provide strong opposition to the right. Defeating the far right can only come from an organized majority of the working class. DSA must fill this vacuum by leading a truly independent, working class fightback. This means fighting back on every level, organizing rank-and-file union workers and tenants, and building militant resistance through street power, strike power, and state power. 12. DSA’s National Political Committee (NPC) created the Trump Administration Response Committee (TARC) with one to two representatives each from the National Labor Commission (NLC), the National Electoral Committee (NEC), the International Committee (IC), the Green New Deal Campaign Commission (GNDCC), the Communications Committee, the Trans Rights and Bodily Autonomy Campaign Commission (TRBACC), and YDSA, with a remit to prepare a response to the Trump administration. 13. 2028 is a pivotal year for socialists, with a presidential election and a call from UAW president Shawn Fain for unions to align their contract expirations on May Day 2028, giving organized workers unprecedented leverage. DSA must be at the forefront of organizing toward these events, understand the potential for mass politicization, and develop a comprehensive strategy to build to this pivotal moment. Only socialism can defeat fascism. Therefore, be it resolved, 1. DSA recognizes Trumpism and the far right as an existential threat that demands a comprehensive, organization-wide strategic response to protect our members, build working class organization and resistance, and prepare for 2028. 2. The TARC shall: 1. Develop and help execute, with the Communications Committee, a cohesive national messaging strategy framing DSA as the alternative to Trumpism and the far right, as well as to the compliant and neoliberal entrenched leadership in the Democratic Party 2. Coordinate national, regional/state level, and chapter level actions to resist right wing policies, including direct actions, mass mobilizations, and coalition work. 3. Conduct training at the national level and for individual chapters on direct action, immigration rapid response, and compliance. 4. Coordinate with other national bodies, including NEC, TRBACC, and GNDCC, to incorporate, where strategic, the ongoing work of those bodies into the messaging and tactics of this campaign. This may include: 1. NEC work, including training chapters to recruit and run candidates. 2. TRBACC work, including legislative and ballot campaigns for trans and abortion rights. 3. GNDCC work on chapter campaigns for social housing, mass transit, public power and green schools, and other organizing that can build local resistance to and power against right-wing agendas. 5. Develop plans and resources along with the Organizational Security Committee (OSC) to help chapters resist state repression, including the following: 1. Conducting “Know Your Rights” training for members facing state or employer retaliation. 2. Conducting security and digital safety training to protect against far right attacks and government surveillance. 3. Along with other relevant national bodies, conducting de-escalation and direct action training to prepare for street confrontations and state repression. 6. Organize mass calls and rapid-response plans in response to new political developments, aimed at providing clear political direction to our response and helping grow the organization. 7. Coordinate actions against Democratic politicians who capitulate to Trump’s policies, harnessing the mass discontent among working class Democratic voters who feel abandoned and are searching for an alternative. 8. Contribute to mass movements defending democracy and support movements that prioritize the mass participation and independence of the working class rather than liberal NGO-driven efforts, continuing the commitments outlined in 2023 MSR #2, Defend Democracy Through Political Independence. 9. Produce a national strategy and work plan by the end of 2025 to coordinate the fight against the far right, involving all relevant national committees and working groups. 1. This will be a priority national campaign, coordinated through TARC and overseen by the NPC, and including all national bodies and chapters. 3. The NPC shall ensure appropriate staff time is directed to aid in coordinating and carrying out this member-led campaign. 4. DSA will launch a national recruitment drive to double membership by 2027. 1. The Growth and Development Committee (GDC) shall oversee this expansion by: 1. Conducting mass recruitment campaigns targeting those radicalized by the Trump administration. 2. Coordinating a chapter mentorship program to onboard and retain new members. 3. Providing technical and organizing support to chapters for digital outreach and organizing tools. 4. Launch a sustained recommitment drive to recontact the ~100k lapsed DSA members, including ones who signed up for the now finally defunct one-time dues option, who account for the largest source of passive membership loss over the past 5 years. 5. Conducting targeted themed recruitment drives to nonmembers on DSA lists and shared from aligned organizations, including EWOC, especially to recruit workers in labor unions and workplace organizing efforts. 5. DSA’s NLC shall, as part of the TARC priority campaign against the far right, coordinate labor resistance efforts against the Trump administration’s anti-worker agenda, including: 1. Organizing rank-and-file campaigns to push for unions to resist Trump administration policies. 2. Building relationships with militant labor organizers, prioritizing strategic sectors, to mobilize the labor movement against Trump’s attacks. 3. Struggling against conservative tendencies within unions and fighting to win rank-and-file workers over to democratic socialist politics 4. Developing contingency plans for a potential rollback of the National Labor Relations Act (NLRA) and the imposition of national right-to-work laws. 5. Organizing current and former federal workers and other public-sector employees as a core constituency for socialist organizing. 1. Collaborating with the Federal Unionists Network (FUN) to: 1. Build an organized, militant layer of workers within federal worker unions. 2. Support whistleblower protections and legal resources for federal workers. 3. Launch public campaigns against the Trump administration’s attempts to privatize government programs and purge the civil service. 4. Coordinate demonstrations and direct actions aimed at putting pressure on Congress to dissolve DOGE and protect federal workers and the beneficiaries of federal policy. 2. Organizing toward a potential general strike on May 1st, 2028 by: 1. Organizing as rank-and-file workers within unions to align their contract expirations for this date and build rank-and-file support for a set of common demands and shared political program for the potential general strike. 2. Building up a “strike ready” campaign modeled on the 2023 NLC UPS Teamsters campaign and subsequent UAW Stand Up Strike campaign. 3. Building DSA as a hub for planning, public campaign visibility, and shared tools for chapters and labor formations participating in strike preparation. 4. Launching a political education and public communications program for DSA members and the public, building toward the potential strike. Full text Whereas the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) aspires to build a mass socialist party rooted in the working class, capable of wielding real political power; Whereas the current national structures and decision-making processes of DSA suffer from opacity, structural barriers to participation, and an over-reliance on insider control, limiting the ability of rank-and-file members to shape the organization’s political direction; Whereas the movement toward a mass socialist party requires deepening democracy within DSA itself, empowering members to meaningfully engage in decision-making at the national level; Whereas DSA must move beyond its current patchwork of decision-making processes and adopt clear, consistent, and participatory mechanisms that reflect the will of the membership as a whole; Whereas mass socialist and working-class parties across the world operate on the principle of One Member, One Vote, a principle generally advocated for by the radical currents within those organizations; Whereas DSA has advocated and will continue to advocate for labor unions to adopt the One Member, One Vote principle; Whereas leadership elections and electoral endorsements within most DSA chapters are held via all-member vote; Whereas the principle of One Member, One Vote (OMOV) for key national decisions will democratize DSA, ensuring that its leadership and political direction are directly accountable to the full membership; Therefore be it resolved that DSA will implement One Member, One Vote for federal endorsements, beginning after the close of the 2025 Convention. Federal endorsements poll will be considered in favor if approved by 60% of members voting. The results of the poll will be published to all members and the general public within 1 week of the close of voting. Be it further resolved that the One Member, One Vote process for federal endorsements will apply to the following elections: * President of the United States * United States Senate * United States House of Representatives Be it further resolved that the NPC will set an endorsement cycle schedule which governs when federal endorsement polls may occur. Be it further resolved that upon submission of a petition of one-third of NPC members, potential federal endorsements shall be referred to the general membership for a One Member, One Vote poll no later than three months after the date the petition was submitted.[12] Be it further resolved that the One Member, One Vote process for federal endorsements will be required for DSA to engage in any express advocacy in any federal election, meaning any activity which urges any person to vote for or vote against any identifiable candidate, including any efforts to urge people to “withhold” votes from or “boycott” a campaign. Be it further resolved that a process be created for all members in good standing to submit statements on endorsement votes, to be included along with electronic ballots sent to members, and that recordings of the discussion forums also be sent along with the electronic ballots. Be it further resolved that the One Member, One Vote process for federal endorsements will be required to rescind any endorsement previously approved by membership through the One Member, One Vote process. Be it finally resolved that this resolution is part of a broader effort to transform DSA into a more democratic, participatory, and member-driven organization—one that is not only capable of influencing federal politics but is also built from the bottom up to serve as a foundation for a mass working-class political party. Status: Adopted Summary Principles for Party-Building are a set of guidelines for the task set out by the 2025 convention’s theme - preparing for a decade of party building. Almost everyone in DSA says they want a party, but most of us mean different things. These ten principles define DSA’s approach as a party surrogate with real political independence, and the values we must hold in establishing a mass socialist party. Full text Whereas, the 2023 DSA convention resolved that “DSA and its local chapters remain committed to the project of building a working-class party: a mass democratic political organization capable of winning and wielding state power with a strategy for social transformation;” and Whereas, multiple conceptions of a working class political party exist in history and the global working class movement; and Whereas, DSA in some senses already performs the functions of a working class party, only lacking its own state-recognized ballot line; and Whereas, the undemocratic US bourgeois political system intentionally places roadblocks in the way of a democratic membership organization controlling its own ballot line; and Whereas, DSA is not just any working class organization but specifically a socialist organization, which fights for the universal and long term interests of the working class for political democracy, general social transformation, and a collectively owned and democratically planned economy, Therefore be it resolved, DSA commits to the goal of becoming an independent mass socialist party, with the following principles: 1. The fundamental purpose of a socialist party is to be a mass association of the working class formed for collective political action. The party will be united around a democratically created program that outlines goals that, enacted together, will allow the working class to rule and end capitalism. 2. The foundation of party democracy is freedom of information, association, and discussion. Members must be able to critique the party’s program and organize to change it, as long as they are willing to accept fighting for it as the democratically-determined expression of DSA’s goals. 3. The internal governing principles of the party must guarantee all members equal right of participation in the democratic process, regular conventions of membership as the highest decision-making body, open leadership elections at conventions, local party organizations run by membership, and the free organization of factions. 4. Guaranteeing members equal right of participation in the democratic process requires that participation be reserved for individual members. Groups may choose to affiliate with DSA on the basis of acceptance of our program, but may not be given voting rights as an organization. 5. Because of an undemocratic and uneven electoral system designed to maintain capitalist rule, DSA fights on unfavorable terrain and is pulled between the necessity of independent political action and using the ballot line of the Democratic Party. DSA’s approach is the party surrogate, acting as a party but without a dedicated ballot line. 6. While DSA must move away from use of the Democratic Party ballot line and primaries, a ballot line is not the primary goal or indication of political independence. What matters most is bringing our independent organization and program to races whether on a Democratic, independent, or third-party ballot line. 7. When considering whether to create a ballot line of our own, losing control of our candidates to an open state-run process is a non-negotiable red line. Our ability to take independent political action is essential to preserve above all other considerations. 8. DSA orients itself in opposition to all ruling class political forces. DSA’s project is to unite workers to win the battle for democracy and bring about socialism, not to seek a governing coalition with a perceived lesser evil under the current undemocratic political system. 9. A socialist party in the United States must be a part of the global political movement of the working class. It is guided by the international interests of the class, not narrow national interests. 10. The socialist movement is strengthened by putting forward common perspectives and engaging in common action internationally. DSA will continue to build ties with socialist parties around the world with the goal of forming a new International. Full Text Whereas a censure is a formal reprimand expressing displeasure at a member’s actions; and Whereas power over endorsed electeds comes primarily from the size and organization of DSA’s membership; and Whereas a vote to censure by the general membership body expresses the displeasure of the majority of rank-and-file members; and Whereas absent a democratic censure process, dissatisfied members of a chapter are unable to make their case to the broader chapter membership; and Whereas a lack of uniformity privileges some members over others based on factors including chapter and leadership position; and Whereas without a uniform and democratic censure process across DSA, members will be unable to exert control over the electoral program, leaving influence over the electeds in the hands of small leadership cliques; Therefore let it be resolved, any member in good standing of a chapter may submit a resolution with greater than or equal to 5% of members in good standing of that chapter to censure an endorsed elected; Resolved, the resolution to censure must be shared with general membership of the chapter and heard at the soonest possible General Meeting or Chapter Convention; Resolved, a motion to censure an elected official requires a majority vote of present and voting members equal to the ratio required for endorsement; Resolved, once passed, the resolution to censure must be announced and publicly posted within 72 hours; Resolved, revocation of endorsement shall follow the same process as a censure; Resolved, the following will be distributed by chapters to membership as the policy for democratic discipline: Any member in good standing may submit a resolution for the general membership to censure or unendorse an elected official endorsed by the chapter. In order to be heard, this resolution requires signatures of 5% of members in good standing at the time of submission or as many signatures as any ordinary business item at a General Meeting or Chapter Convention, whichever is fewer. The censure resolution must be shared with the full membership and heard at the next General Meeting or Chapter Convention. A motion to censure or unendorse an endorsed elected official requires a majority vote of present members to pass. If the censure passes, the resolution must be publicly posted within 72 hours. If there is no chapter meeting or convention scheduled within 90 days of turning in a resolution of this type with signatures from 5% of members in good standing, a special meeting will be called to be held within 30 days. External links Original forum submission: https://discussion.dsausa.org/t/41447 R09: For Political and Technological Independence: A Path to Exit from Capitalist and Democratic Party Tech Submitted by Colin M (North New Jersey), Jen M (Eugene-Springfield), Derrick L (San Francisco), Brian D (Metro DC), Ian H (Chicago), John L (New Orleans), Andrew C (Chicago), Amy W (Seattle), Alex S (Austin). Status: Adopted Summary DSA has relied on off-the-shelf tech tools from both our class enemies as well as political enemies in order to meet the needs of our work. Despite the contradictions of this, no plan has been put in place on how to stop using these tools or even prepare for the day where we’re locked out of using them for good due to political positions we take. This resolution aims to be the implementation plan for our tech, to build us up as an independent party, done thoughtfully and on our terms. Full text Whereas, DSA from 2016 to now has had to quickly scale to meet the political moment with our technology stack, largely relying on off the shelf capitalist tools like Google Suite (GSuite) and Airtable along with entering into pricing discounts for technology made by Democratic Party consultants with fellow “movement” organizations via The Movement Cooperative (TMC) for tools like Voter Action Network (VAN) and ActionKit (our National membership database). DSA National historically has only purchased technology for itself, very rarely does it filter down to Chapters and Committees beyond the essentials and even then it’s sporadic (e.g. email not being universally provided to DSA bodies). Chapters are left to themselves, spending additional dues money on technology that duplicates National expenses and may differ in tool selection for no reason other than it’s not provided holistically by the National organization. This has fragmented how comrades interact with and build DSA locally, where no one chapter appears to be following best practices between each other. While we continue to lead as the largest socialist organization in the United States, we’ve inherited political and financial risks of tying ourselves to tools reliant on Democratic Party consultants. We risk losing access to tools we pay for from political positions we take: Running against incumbent Democrats has denied us access to VAN in some races in the past. DSA has been denied access to technology by companies or organizations unwilling to allow socialists to use their platforms or products. After October 7th we saw “abuse bombing” disrupt the online presence for several allied organizations (JVP, PYM, SJP) against their public copies of Palestine toolkits hosted on capitalist technology. These are concerns we will run into until we are operationally independent, and, as outlined by Act Like an Independent Party, why DSA must build these things ourselves. Aside from political concerns, these technology consultants are on shaky ground with layoffs affecting their staff and decline in quality of their product even to the point of the Democratic National Committee (DNC) attempting to exercise contractual rights to take over certain tools along TMC now looking to develop alternative tooling, turning a potential shakeup into a game of musical chairs that DSA could be locked out of. We however, look past the market to tools that we own or are owned by our allies, instead of temporary partnerships with our class and political enemies. Therefore, be it resolved, The National Tech Committee (NTC) shall conduct a yearly software audit, to be completed no later than October 31 of each calendar year, with the exception of a 2025 audit to be completed by December 31, 2025. DSA Staff is directed to provide any and all information necessary to complete the audit. The audit shall include, but is not limited to: * An assessment of replacement feasibility for all software. Considerations shall include, but are not limited to: * Contract terms * Implementation and impact assessment * Existing DSA software ecosystem compatibility * Ability to scale usage to DSA national bodies, chapters, and/or members * Recommendations for alternative solutions where feasible * A survey of current software usage * Cost analysis for all software No later than December 31, 2025, the NTC shall produce, in consultation with DSA staff: * A software procurement and asset management process * A rubric for determining when an NTC recommendation shall be required for the acquisition of software solutions. See Appendix for an example rubric. * A plan for provisioning access to DSA software tools for further development by chapters and members (e.g. API access). The NTC shall be directed to submit a comprehensive plan for strategic software replacement(s) for approval by the NPC. This plan shall include, but is not limited to: * By the end of Q2 2026: * A report outlining the replacement feasibility of any DSA technology currently purchased through “movement organization” providers (e.g. ActionKit - DSA’s Membership Database Tool) or other Democratic Party consultants. * An assessment of DSA hosting capability. For tools that may not be feasible to host at cost with member labor, contracting hosting providers should be explored with the following goals: * Company makeup: is the hosting provider a worker-owned cooperative? If not, are its staff unionized? If not, are they a “good steward”[14] for the tool? * Open source availability: is the product open source? If not, is there no other alternative that can be used that is? * By the end of Q4 2026: * Migration plan and project timeline for selected strategic software replacement(s), to be implemented by December 31, 2027. Appendix: DSA Technology Purchasing Rubric The following are submitted as the minimum questions that need to be included in any final copy of a Tech purchasing Rubric that Staff and the NTC will work on developing. These include questions to assess a Tool’s company background, industry standard security assessment questions, whether or not the tool is Open Source or there’s known Open Source alternatives, labor and labor related questions, and external political questions ranging from Democratic Party relationships, Tool Background: Tool Name Tool Provider Scope: National Office, National Committees, Chapters, or All? Contract terms Security: Hosting Location, SOC 2 Type 2 Attestation Have there been any recent public data breaches? What’s their infosec policy for customers? Free/Open Source Software Is the Tool Open Source? Are there any known alternatives? Are the alternatives Open Source? Company background: Company Makeup: Startup? Subsidiary of a larger company? Likely to be acquired? Worker-Owned? If the company is not worker-owned, are the employees unionized? Funding: Are they a public or private company? VC Funded? Non-Profit? Labor Is the tool possible to self-host via NTC? If possible to self-host, is this core infrastructure that DSA should find hosting for? If not possible to self-host, is the Tool Provider the hosting provider? If not direct from the Tool Provider, Is the Hosting Provider involved in the Tool Ecosystem (e.g. Open Source development, community workshops and trainings)[15] Is there an API or other way of interacting with the tool for NTC development and/or interaction to help improve the tool or improve its adoption? External Political Conditions AI: Do they harvest our data for AI training? Is it their own engine or another provider? Is there an opt-out? Is there any known relationship with the Democratic (or Republican) Party? Is there any known relationship with the US DoD or other intelligence apparatus? Is there any known use by allied organizations? Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions: Are they on the BDS list? Do they work in any way with the Israeli Government? Are they located in Israel? Do they have a well known capitalist backer behind the tool? Full text Whereas, in line with 2017 DSA National Convention Resolutions #7 and #8, and 2019 Resolution #35, DSA unapologetically stands in solidarity with the Palestinian people; and is committed to the Boycott, Divestment, and Sanctions (BDS) movement; Whereas, since March 25th 2025, 54 DSA chapters representing over 30,000 DSA members have passed their own versions of the “Make DSA an Anti-Zionist Organization in Principle and Praxis” resolution, enshrining locally both membership expectations and electoral endorsement conditions of principled anti-Zionism that has provided a necessary, material counter-weight to the Zionist lobby for progressives running for local office; Whereas, DSA has recognized Zionism as “a racist, imperialist, settler-colonial project that has resulted in the ongoing death, displacement, and dehumanization of Palestinians everywhere,” whose survival is enabled by the financial, military, and diplomatic support of the United States government; Whereas, as repression against the Palestine solidarity movement by the Trump administration, universities, and other aligned institutions escalates, mobilizing our electoral project, our position in the labor movement, and our organizational density in the education sector to build more favorable terrain for organizing and resist state repression is necessary to meet the current moment; Whereas, since March 2025, the National Labor Commission (NLC) adopted a resolution forming a Labor for an Arms Embargo campaign working group and the IC Palestine Subcommittee adopted a political education proposal for webinars on municipal divestment; Whereas, carrying out the obligations of pro-Palestine and BDS convention mandates requires clear goals for Palestine solidarity work and a renewed commitment to being productive coalition partners within the wider Palestinian solidarity movement; Standards and Orientation Therefore, be it resolved, that DSA shall make organizing in solidarity with the Palestinian cause a priority until Palestine is free, unequivocally affirming our commitment to ‘al-Thawabit’, the principles originally set by the Palestinian National Council in 1977 and repeatedly reaffirmed since, which are the Palestinian people’s right to resistance, the Palestinian right to self-determination, the recognition of Jerusalem as the capital of Palestine, and the right of Palestinian refugees to return to their homeland from the river to the sea; Be it resolved, that DSA shall expand on the expectations, established by the “Make DSA an Anti-Zionist Organization in Principle and Praxis” resolution ratified by the 2023-2025 NPC, that DSA candidates support the BDS movement, refrain from any and all affiliation with the Israeli government or Zionist lobby groups, and pledge to oppose legislation that harms Palestinians and support legislation that supports Palestinian liberation, by affirming that these commitments as detailed in this resolution must hold true for all candidates endorsed by national DSA or a DSA chapter; Be it resolved, that any candidate questionnaires used to determine national and local endorsements must inquire about the candidateʼs position on BDS and should include further scrutiny on the candidate’s commitment to Palestinian liberation; Be it resolved, that potential candidates who cannot commit to the aforementioned basic expectations shall be deemed, by the National Electoral Commission as well as any relevant approving bodies at the chapter level, as ineligible for endorsement by DSA or a DSA chapter; Be it resolved, that, upon receiving fair and ample opportunity for education about the Palestinian struggle for liberation, endorsed candidates who fail to continue to uphold the aforementioned basic expectations after being endorsed and/or taking office, shall have their DSA endorsements revoked locally and/or nationally as applicable; Be it resolved, that DSA members – regardless of endorsement status – who are credibly shown to: 1. have consistently and publicly opposed BDS and the Palestinian cause (e.g. by denouncing the BDS movement in public interviews; writing public op-eds denouncing the BDS movement; drafting and voting in favor of legislation that suppresses BDS, such as legislation that suppresses speech rights around the right to freely criticize Zionism/Israel and/or the right to boycott; making statements that “Israel has a right to defend itself”; making or endorsing statements or legislation equating anti-Zionism with antisemitism), even after receiving fair and ample opportunity for education about the Palestinian struggle for liberation, 2. be currently affiliated with the Israeli government or any Zionist lobby group(s) such as, but not limited to, AIPAC, J Street, or Democratic Majority for Israel (DMFI), or 3. have knowingly provided material aid to Israel (e.g., voted to provide Israel with material aid; gave direct financial donations of any kind to Israel and/or settler NGOs who carry out the mission of Israeli settlement and Palestinian dispossession/displacement, such as the Jewish National Fund, the Israel Land Fund, the Hebron Fund, and Regavim) shall be considered in substantial disagreement with DSAʼs principles and policies, as per Article 1, Section 3 of the DSA Bylaws, thereby committing an expellable offense as outlined in Article 3, Section 4 of the DSA Constitution, which states that a member credibly shown to have engaged in any of the above may “be expelled [by] a two-thirds (⅔) vote of all members of the National Political Committee”; Be it resolved, that DSA shall continue to organize chapters and national bodies to act as meaningful partners within the Palestine solidarity movement, prioritizing campaigns and organizing approaches that: 1. Directly undermine material support for Israel, respond to priorities identified by the Palestinian solidarity movement, and correspond with strategic organizing sectors where DSA is well-positioned to contribute (e.g. logistics and higher education); 2. Build an organized mass base of support for Palestine and engage a range of political and mass organizations, communities, and economic sectors, thus bringing working-class people together through joint struggle and strengthening our local and national coalitions, particularly with Palestinian-led organizations; 3. Protect our movement and build resilience against state and Zionist repression; Build in Coalitions Be it resolved, that DSA reaffirms its commitment to the Stop Fueling Genocide campaign, encourages chapters to identify whether a local campaign is viable, and directs the IC Palestine Subcommittee to continue to expand the number of chapters involved in Stop Fueling Genocide, with a goal of having at least one active campaign in each of the top 15 states with the most Chevron gas stations by the end of 2026; Be it resolved, that DSA endorses the Palestine Solidarity Working Group’s No Appetite For Apartheid (NA4A) campaign, encourages all chapters to identify whether running a local campaign is viable, and directs the IC Palestine Subcommittee and the National Communications Committee to share information about the NA4A campaign with chapters and members and to publicize NA4A campaign calls, announcements, victories, and calls to action as they occur; Be it resolved, that the IC Palestine Subcommittee shall conduct targeted outreach to chapters located in states other than the 15 states where local NA4A campaigns are active as of April 2025, with the goal of organizing chapters in at least 12 new states to launch a local campaign by the end of 2026; Be it resolved, that DSA endorses the Palestinian Youth Movement’s Mask Off Maersk campaign and reaffirms its commitment to leveraging its members’ presence in the labor movement to build labor support for arms embargo campaigns such as Mask off Maersk and No Harbor for Genocide by growing the Labor for an Arms Embargo working group within the NLC, as outlined in the March 2025 NLC resolution; Be it resolved, that the Labor for an Arms Embargo working group shall work toward an initial goal of kickstarting campaigns to support an arms embargo in at least 10 union locals in strategic cities (i.e., cities with seaports, airports, and inland logistics hubs implicated in transporting military cargo to Israel or cities with Maersk terminals) by the end of 2026; Be it resolved, that the Mask Off Maersk organizing committee within the IC Palestine Subcommittee shall identify a minimum of 5 chapters in or closest to strategic cities as defined above or in locations where there is no pre-existing PYM chapter already spearheading Maersk organizing and, by the end of 2026, recruit them to support campaigns in union locals with parallel community organizing, including: 1. Attacking Maersk’s institutional ties by pressuring suppliers, universities, cultural institutions, and other organizations to terminate partnerships, sponsorships, contracts, and research collaborations with Maersk; 2. Increasing reputational damage to Maersk by exposing its participation in genocide through media engagement, public events, and community education; 3. participation in efforts to disrupt weapons shipments, such as Block the Boat; coalitional relationships with relevant organizations), for a total of 9 members, which shall meet at least quarterly to provide coordination and develop joint strategies across different bodies; Be it resolved, that the IC Palestine Subcommittee and Arms Embargo Steering Committee shall produce a short report to membership by March 2027 evaluating the successes, challenges, and overall effectiveness of DSA’s participation in the Stop Fueling Genocide, NA4A, and Arms Embargo campaigns, assessing the status of these efforts, and recommending updated goals, strategies, and relationship to these campaigns to be adopted by 2027 convention; Be it resolved, that candidates endorsed by DSA shall be asked to vote in favor of legislation that directly advances the goals of DSA-endorsed campaigns related to Palestinian liberation, such as Mask off Maersk, Stop Fueling Genocide, No Appetite for Apartheid, and Not On Our Dime and refrain from public disavowal of such campaigns; BDS from City Council to the Union Hall Be it resolved, that, building on the IC Palestine Subcommittee’s political education series on Municipal Level Divestment Campaigns, DSA shall continue to develop chapters’ ability to undertake divestment campaigns targeting direct investments in Israel (e.g. Israeli bonds); investments in companies complicit in Israeli apartheid and genocide; and investments in the war industry more broadly including Maersk, through the following capacity-building blocks: 1. Developing a framework to analyze local conditions and opportunities to identify whether a divestment campaign is strategic; 2. Training chapters on campaign strategy and target identification for pressure campaigns and ballot initiatives; 3. Producing or collecting template language for divestment resolutions, ordinances, and ballot initiatives tailored for different institutions including city councils, faith organizations, labor unions, pension funds, educational and cultural organizations, etc.; Be it resolved, that the NLC shall provide support and coordination, including sharing resolution template language, for DSA members to kickstart or support efforts for labor unions to divest from companies and institutions complicit in Israeli occupation and apartheid or broadly adopt BDS principles, if dealing with union locals that are not strategically well positioned for an arms embargo-focused campaign; Be it resolved, that, in coordination with the IC Palestine Subcommittee, the National Electoral Commission and local chapters’ Socialists in Office or similar formations shall provide template language and direct DSA-endorsed elected officials to advance and support municipal ordinances and local ballot measures that push municipalities or states to adopt divestment and/or other commitments to advance an arms embargo, synthesizing lessons and tools from recent case studies (e.g., the Apartheid-Free Community ballot measures passed by 5 towns in Vermont) as well as historical precedents (e.g., the nuclear-free zones movement and the South Africa Apartheid boycott and divestment movement); Be it resolved, that DSA shall work toward an initial goal of kickstarting organizing around ballot initiatives in at least 5 chapters by the end of 2026, ideally in jurisdictions where efforts can develop in coordination with DSA-endorsed elected officials, as a structure test to pilot the ballot initiative divestment strategy; Be it resolved, that the IC Palestine Subcommittee and the National Electoral Commission shall produce a short report to membership in early 2027, evaluating the successes, challenges, and lessons learnt from these pilot campaigns and recommending updated goals for divestment strategies to be adopted by 2027 convention; Be it resolved, that the National Electoral Commission, Federal Socialists in Office Committee, and local chapters’ Socialists in Office committees or equivalent formations shall support DSA-endorsed elected officials in providing template language for legislation that: * Advances civil rights protections for Palestine solidarity organizing and counters repression of the movement, including commitments from city councils, state legislatures, and other relevant state agencies to: 1. Decline to share data with federal law enforcement and federal agencies; 2. End joint surveillance initiatives with the federal government (e.g., ‘anti-terrorism task forces’, fusion centers, etc.); 3. Refuse to assist federal law enforcement and federal troops in the policing and surveillance of protests; 4. Resist the deployment of National Guard troops to suppress protests. * Repeals laws and policies that limit our ability to organize and expose us to state repression, such as anti-BDS laws, the IHRA definitions of anti-semitism, or anti-masking laws; * Opposes efforts to penalize individuals, universities, and other entities that boycott or protest Israel, including actions that permit the use of force by the state against people protesting in support of Palestine, harming Palestinians and their allies and violating rights to freedom of speech and expression; Support the Student Intifada Be it resolved, that DSA shall provide the YDSA Palestine Committee with staff time and liaisons from the National Communications Committee, IC Palestine Subcommittee, and NLC as needed; Be it resolved, that DSA affirms support for YDSA’s ‘Sanctuary Campus’ national priority campaign and shall facilitate coordination between the YDSA National Coordinating Committee and the NLC, IC Migrant Rights Working Group, and IC Palestine Subcommittee to develop joint strategies for students, higher education workers, and community members in order to win protections for immigrant students and workers and fight political repression of Palestine solidarity organizers on campus; Be it resolved, that DSA shall, through the IC Palestine Subcommittee and other relevant national bodies involved in rapid response organizing, facilitate access to legal representation, jail support, and compliance advice for any DSA and YDSA members facing disciplinary repercussions or repression at their universities and workplaces or prosecution by the state due to their involvement in Palestine solidarity organizing. R24: To Defeat Trump, Turn Toward the Masses Submitted by Aspen W (New Orleans), Sam L (NYC-DSA), Stella T (Boston). Qualified on May 4, 2025, with 303 signatures as of May 11, 2025. Status: Referred to NPC Summary Our primary task at this moment is to defeat the far right. To do this, this resolution proposes taking a nonsectarian approach to uniting with groups that are mobilizing working people into action to protect lives and democratic rights. Even as we work together, we will contest for socialist leadership of the anti-fascist front’s strategy. DSA will demonstrate that socialist politics and organization are the best path forward for striking blows against the capitalist class and the far right. Full text Whereas, since January 2025, the far right controls the levers of state power in the United States on the federal level and in many states; Whereas, the far right has undertaken a rapid and dramatic consolidation of power and push toward authoritarianism, undermining labor rights and cancelling union contracts; disappearing and persecuting protestors, immigrants, and trans people; and flouting the rule of law; Whereas, the far right enjoys enormous material resources, including the support of the richest men in the world, who are beneficiaries of its policies; Whereas, socialists cannot contest for state power in the United States without building a working-class movement large enough to overcome the material advantages of the far right; Whereas, such a movement necessarily includes millions of people who do not yet identify as democratic socialists; Whereas, to raise the consciousness of the masses and win people to socialism, socialists must mobilize and be active participants in mass movements of the people; Whereas, to defeat the far right, socialists must not downplay its threat; must confront it directly as a central opponent; must offer a strong alternative vision to win workers away from the fascist temptation, while also simultaneously and as part of this strategy contesting for leadership through aggressive challenge to the corporate centrism that has seeded the ground for its rise; Therefore be it resolved, DSA recognizes that our primary task in the current political moment is to defeat the far right, and that mobilization and organization of masses of people will be necessary to defeat the right, as well as to take the next steps toward winning socialism; Be it further resolved, DSA will orient toward the masses over the next two years by building the largest possible opposition to the Trump administration and taking a nonsectarian approach to uniting with unions, the women’s movement, organizations of people of color, organizations of immigrants, and any mass organizations committed to resisting the advance of the right; Be it further resolved, DSA will engage with the working class where people are in motion. We will immerse ourselves in the mass movements that are increasingly resisting the encroachment of the authoritarian right. Our goal will be to build unity with masses of people around a democratic socialist strategy that can have a broad and profound impact and expand our socialist project; Be it further resolved, DSA recognizes the importance of the organizations mobilizing masses of people into opposition right now against the Trump administration, such as the Federal Unionists Network (FUN), Indivisible, and Center for Popular Democracy. They are doing vital work in opposing the country’s slide into fascism. They are also, in a general sense, more liberal rather than socialist in political orientation. We commit to a willingness to work in coalition with these and similar groups when feasible, even where we have political differences, on the core criterion that they are bringing masses of hitherto non-politicized working people into action, and that in working with them we are not required to subordinate our own socialist politics; Be it further resolved, DSA commends Bernie Sanders’ and Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez’s work on the “Fighting Oligarchy” tour, and its work of providing socialist leadership and activating hundreds of thousands of people out to fight. We will collaborate wherever feasible with the tour’s work, including promoting it, providing logistical support if needed, and being on site with materials to help bring attendees into long-term political organization; Be it further resolved, DSA recognizes that we cannot tail elected officials, other organizations, or public opinion, nor subordinate the case for a working-class strategy in coalitions. We believe socialist leadership is necessary to win against the far-right tide and that the path to defeating fascism lies in rooting out the corporate politics of both parties and building working-class, democratic, and confrontational organizations. Even as we work with other groups on the shared goal of defeating the right, we will remain committed to contesting for socialist leadership of the working class and carrying out a working class strategy. Be it further resolved, DSA will fight for leadership of the masses by challenging and defeating corporate Democrats, by leading the fight for material gains in mass organizations like labor unions and tenant unions, by spreading socialist ideas, by fighting for materials wins and non-reformist reforms, for racial justice, gender justice, and immigrant justice, and by acting in solidarity with working people and all people facing attacks from the far right; Be it further resolved, DSA will continue our strategy of leading concerted and confrontational efforts to elect socialists in US primaries, and will continue to avoid a strategy in general election races that creates a significant chance of “spoiling” elections to allow far right victories with a minority of the vote; Be it further resolved, DSA recognizes the essential role chapters in rural areas and “red” and “purple” districts have to play in building a broad nationwide front against fascism, and will especially support these chapters in efforts to orient toward mass-movement work that connects with people in the thousands and millions; Be it finally resolved, DSA will demonstrate in practice and through mutual struggle that socialist politics and organization are the best path forward for striking blows against the capitalist class and the far right. Qualified on May 4, 2025, with 304 signatures as of May 11, 2025. Status: Referred to NPC Summary Democratic socialism represents a distinct and meaningful political tradition. This resolution lays out some of its fundamental principles and aspirations to end capitalist and imperialist oppression and to bring the institutions of political, economic, and social life under popular and truly democratic control; the democratic socialist theory of change; and the broad coalitions of the democratic left, undergirded by mass working-class organization. Full text Whereas, democratic socialism represents a distinct and meaningful political tradition; Whereas, as a democratic socialist organization with a welcoming, open, mass, and nonsectarian character, DSA should define, in broad terms, what democratic socialism is so that millions of people can join the organization with confidence in its overall mission; therefore be it Resolved that the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) affirms its identity as a democratic socialist organization along the following lines: 1. Democratic socialism is the movement to end capitalist and imperialist oppression and bring the institutions of political, economic, and social life under popular and truly democratic control; 2. This movement must activate a majority of the population and build popular capacity to govern the economy, civil society, and the State, and thus its aims must be achieved through democratic means. 3. The political basis of this movement will be a mass working class organization building a coalition of the democratic left based on labor, environmental, racial justice, feminist, queer, immigrant, peace, anti-imperialist, and faith organizations and people of democratic and progressive conscience. 4. This movement therefore orients toward bringing millions into action and building large working-class-based coalitions, rather than orienting its political appeal to the narrow swathe of the already radicalized. 5. The democratic socialist movement must be led by mass working-class organizations, but works to build political coalitions with other social groups on the basis of common interests and common values. 6. The fight against racism, sexism, anti-queer bigotry, national chauvinism, religious discrimination, and every form of social oppression is both morally righteous and essential to the political unification of the working class and the democratic left. 7. The democratic socialist movement is profoundly ecological, understands that environmental exploitation is inherent to capitalism, and therefore is fully dedicated to the global fight for a just transition to avert climate and ecological catastrophe. 8. Democratic socialists demand an end to anti-democratic, imperialist intervention by the US government in other countries, especially in the Global South, which has led to massive human and natural resource exploitation, the toppling of popular regimes, and even genocide around the world, and stand in solidarity with global left social movements and political parties fighting for self-determination, human rights, radical democracy and inclusive sustainable development. 9. Democratic socialists enter defensive alliances to stop the further political and electoral advance of fascism, while also simultaneously fighting to complete the work of the abolitionists, Reconstruction, the labor movement, the civil rights movement, and the peace movement to demolish the military-industrial complex, to move beyond economic exploitation and capitalism, and to transform the United States into a true political and economic democracy. 10. Specifically democratic socialist organizations with a welcoming, open, mass and nonsectarian character are required to cohere activists, facilitate popular education, and transmit a vision of a truly free, substantively equal, radically democratic post-capitalist society. Be it finally resolved, that DSA will work to orient current and future members to this conception of democratic socialism and communicate it to the general public in the US and abroad. Status: Adopted Summary Escalating fascist repression by the Trump Administration is the most urgent existential threat to the socialist movement in the current political moment. Recent years have shown that mass abolitionist organizing has been a key point of activation within the working class. In order for DSA to effectively lead in the fight against fascism, this resolution presents three strategic points: a national ‘Abolish ICE’ campaign; local abolitionist organizing; and strengthening organizational security. Full Text Whereas, Donald Trump and the Republican Party have made clear their intentions to conduct the "largest deportation operation in history,” criminalize political dissent and advocacy (including threats and campaigns to prosecute immigration lawyers, Black Lives Matter activists, climate organizers, and pro-Palestine protesters as “terrorists”), institute political purges using Schedule F, defund universities that refuse to crack down on Palestine solidarity protests, and a litany of other repressive actions that constitute a fascist agenda in the United States; Whereas, attacks on immigrant Palestinian solidarity activists like Mahmoud Khalil and Momodou Taal and immigrant rights advocates like Jeanette Vizguerra are the cornerstone of the fascist agenda to crush dissent and destroy any pretense of civil rights and a continuation of a legacy of repression of movements deemed hostile to US imperialism extending back to the Holy Land Five, Leonard Peltier, and beyond; Whereas, U.S. Immigrations and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is part of a fascist strategy that unjustly treats immigrants as criminal threats to the nation and national identity, separates poor immigrant families, and perpetuates a culture of fear and oppression intended to chill dissent against the state; Whereas, the criminalization of immigrants and the expansion of ICE’s powers under both Democratic and Republican administrations have violated human rights and utilized illegal, repressive tactics including detention, deportation, and violence against immigrant communities; Whereas, at its height, the DREAMer movement and organizing for DACA pioneered a range of pressure tactics including high-profile hunger strikes, occupations, and protests to shut down detention centers; Whereas, racial capitalism is the primary motivator for the currently escalating fascism both in the United States and globally (e.g. the oppression of pro-Palestinian activism meant to protect imperial US interests in the Middle East, the proliferation of the for-profit prison industry as a means for elites to gain wealth from human misery, etc.); Whereas, per its 2021 political platform, the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) supports abolishing the police, ICE, and the carceral state; Whereas, DSA recognizes that the fight against fascism and for the right to political expression is inseparable from the fight for immigrant justice, and that defending the rights of immigrants is a cornerstone of anti-fascist struggle; Whereas, mass abolitionist organizing against police brutality and state repression, such as the George Floyd uprising, the Stop Cop City movement, and the 'Sanctuary Campus' campaign led by YDSA and National Students for Justice in Palestine (NSJP) demonstrate that the abolitionist movement continues to be an inspiring source of popular consciousness and a point of activation against fascism within the working class; Whereas, as socialists, we know that the only way to overcome fascism and escalating state repression is decisive and coordinated collective mass action and militant organizing within the working class and labor, social, and student movements; Therefore, be it resolved, that DSA will develop a robust national priority ‘Abolish ICE’ 2025-2027 campaign directed to: 1. Develop national Know Your Rights (KYR) materials available in the eight most commonly spoken languages in the United States that (a) offer citizen and non-citizen members regularly updated guidance about their rights, (b) suggest best practices to maintain operational and personal security in the face of rising fascism, (c) are regularly updated by a team of legal professionals and organizers with insight into relational support and communications, including representatives from the most impacted groups, such as immigrants and activists, and (d) identify capitalism, imperialism, and illegal US-backed sanctions as the root causes of immigration from the global south; 2. Develop a shared resource hub housing trainings on local power mapping, direct action, and other organizing tasks that can also be distributed to chapters organizing around abolitionist demands; 3. Support chapters organizing around ‘sanctuary city’ and ‘sanctuary state’ demands by helping to draft language for legislative resolutions introduced by DSA-endorsed elected officials, and support the NSJP-YDSA ‘Sanctuary Campus’ national priority campaign; 4. Enumerate learnings from successful immigrants rights/defense coalition efforts (e.g. CIRC in Colorado) into resources for chapters navigating coalitional migrant defense organizing; 5. Develop a toolkit for chapters to build local migrant defense coalitions and recruit & train members for migrant defense organizing, including KYR trainings, ICE Watch, rapid response coordination, and legal defense work; 6. Participate in national and local coalitions centered around the demand of abolishing ICE; and 7. Publish an analysis of the campaign prior to the 2027 convention via DSA’s publications highlighting successes, failures, and future work. Be it further resolved, that the National Political Committee (NPC) will select an ‘Abolish ICE’ campaign Steering Committee comprising 11 members: six members elected from an open application process by Single Transferable Vote as well as one liaison each (for a total of five) from the IC Migrant Rights Working Group, YDSA National Coordinating Committee, National Abolition Working Group, National Electoral Commission, and Mutual Aid Working Group, with priority given to members with lived immigration experience and born outside the US; Be it further resolved, that DSA will, through the relevant national bodies, support chapters in building local and state-level campaigns around abolitionist demands, such as: 1. Fighting for ‘non-reformist’ reforms that challenge the core function of the state, such as ending cash bail, increasing court transparency, cutting police budgets, and eliminating mandatory minimums; 2. Recruiting and running the electoral campaigns of explicitly abolitionist cadre candidates in service of an abolitionist and socialist electoral project; 3. Building coalitions with local abolitionist organizations, such as racial justice, immigrants’ rights, prisoner solidarity, and labor groups; 4. Creating public directories of resources including aligned legal advocates, mutual aid, case management, and other relevant support for undocumented or detained Americans and their families; 5. Developing programs of solidarity with incarcerated individuals (including, but not limited to, political prisoners and immigration detainees) within local prisons or ICE detention facilities through means of letter writing, visitation, and direct material support. Be it further resolved, that DSA will, with the support of YDSA and input of non-citizen members solicited by the NPC, create the Collective Defense Fund for the purpose of providing as-needed disbursements to chapters, aligned organizations, and other individuals for legal service or cash bail costs, alternative housing for suspended student protestors or undocumented students, or any other services relevant to abolitionist organizing deemed valuable by the NPC; Be it further resolved, that communications to members regarding resources available to chapters through the Collective Defense Fund and Abolish ICE campaign shall be issued to membership quarterly through the DSA co-chair newsletter and national social media; Be it further resolved, that DSA will prioritize broad, coalitional mass organizing with other groups in the progressive and Palestine solidarity movement spaces against the fascist Republican agenda through means such as mass demonstrations, direct actions, and strikes similar to the Inauguration Day ‘We Fight Back’ actions and the April 5 ‘March on Washington’ Day of Action, and the NPC will create a toolkit for anti-fascist messaging in conjunction with chapters and national bodies; Be it further resolved, that the NPC, National Communications Committee, and National Political Education Committee will coordinate independent DSA analysis of the escalating fascist repression of the Trump Administration, as well as organizing tasks for socialists and the working class under Trump, encompassing spaces for internal (e.g., Discussion Board, facilitated discussion circles) and external (e.g., competing pieces in Democratic Left or Socialist Forum) member deliberation and public-facing communications in the form of pitched op-eds to media outlets; Be it further resolved, that the NPC shall provide a status update on the ‘Strengthening Organizational Security’ section of the Strengthening and Expanding DSA: Navigating the Post-2024 Election Landscape Resolution by October 30, 2025 and provide a timeline for the completion of the parts not yet enacted; Be it further resolved, that Red Rabbits will collaborate with the NPC to expand the number of chapters capable of self-sustaining post-protest jail support organizing and community defense through a coaching and chapter liaison program; Be it further resolved, that the National Abolition Working Group and Red Rabbits will, with the input of local chapters, submit a report to the NPC within three months of this resolution’s passage detailing immediately actionable steps that DSA can take on local, regional, and national levels to better prepare the organization for a national uprising against federal agents and police brutality. Capacity Commitment & Financial Impact Scores Capacity 4: High Finances 2: $5000 to $10,000 This resolution received a 4 for Capacity Commitment due to the high level of sustained coordination and member involvement required to implement a multi-year, national-scale campaign centered on abolitionist and migrant defense organizing. The resolution mandates the development of multilingual materials, a shared resource hub for local organizing, legislative support for sanctuary campaigns, and the creation of a Steering Committee with liaisons from multiple national bodies, as well as the formation of the Collective Defense Fund, and other tasks. The scope of this resolution demands high levels of ongoing coordination between staff, the NPC, YDSA, Mutual Aid, IC Migrant Rights, and chapters, especially in rural or contested areas. The inclusion of legal professionals, organizers, and representatives from impacted communities further increases the complexity of implementation. It received a 2 for Financial Impact due to the moderate financial outlay associated with implementing the resolution, including legal advice and coordination as well as potential translation needs. This score assumes that the Collective Defense Fund will be raised externally and not drawn from DSA’s general budget, minimizing direct financial strain on the organization. It also assumes that DSA National will not directly fund legal defense efforts of individuals, but rather disbursements will be made through chapters and outside organizations, reducing legal and compliance risks. R27: Staff Relationship to Members in a Democratic Organization Submitted by: Laura W (Portland), Kristin S (Mid Hudson Valley), Alex P (NYC), Hayley BB (Portland). Qualified on May 4, 2025, with 330 signatures as of May 11, 2025. Status: Adopted Summary This resolution clarifies the political role of staff and their relationship to members and elected member-leaders. Staff make members more collectively self-sufficient, and the NPC has the greatest responsibility in ensuring that! Full Text Whereas, * DSA employs dozens of staff to help carry out the democratically-decided priorities of members and elected leaders. * Staff are a valuable resource that enable the stability and day-to-day function of DSA to an extent that would not be feasible with unpaid member labor alone. * Staff have some special resources, privileges, and platforms that most members do not have. This can present a challenge to DSA’s internal democracy when staff are also tasked with carrying out decisions of the organization that they personally may not agree with. * The NPC is the highest authority between conventions and has the greatest responsibility in ensuring accountability to our priorities and values in the allocation of staff resources. * In the years to come, as in years prior, the NPC will be regularly charged with making decisions about hiring, staff work, and the budget.

Resolved, * DSA affirms that the role of staff is to make members more collectively self-sufficient to deliberate democratically and pursue our mission and priorities. * All DSA staff are encouraged to participate in political deliberation and exchange of ideas in DSA and state their views openly, provided they do not use the special resources available to them in their role as staff to organize members towards positions that are not already the policy of DSA. * Whenever feasible, DSA will ensure that the resources, knowledge, and skills available to staff are made available to members. * When hiring staff, DSA will prioritize considering applicants who share the understanding of the role of staff as laid out in this resolution and who have a history of participation and leadership in DSA nationally or their chapter. The NPC will proactively recruit applicants from chapters and national committees for all vacancies. * When assigning work to staff and overseeing that work, DSA Directors and Managers should seek guidance from democratically-selected member-leaders, particularly National Co-chairs and the NPC. * There shall be no official record of national DSA that NPC (either the whole body or a portion, as determined by the NPC) cannot access.
