R29: Proposal to Launch a Member-Led National Design Committee Submitted by Kristin S (Mid-Hudson Valley DSA). Qualified on May 5, 2025, with 323 signatures as of May 11, 2025. Status: Adopted Summary This proposal launches a member-led design committee that restores member control over branding and art for DSA. Full text Whereas: DSA previously had a National Design Committee that produced a style guide and artistic and branding resources for the organization, but it has not been active in years. Whereas: DSA and our chapters would benefit from re-establishing a national committee to produce artistic and branding resources in order to promote DSA’s visibility with consistent, high-quality materials. Therefore be it resolved, DSA shall establish a National Design Committee (NDC) that is tasked with developing design resources for use across the organization for merch, literature, protest materials, banners, social media and any other materials that require graphics or design. Be it resolved, the committee shall also be tasked with establishing a National Design Resource Center that makes available for chapter and national use all DSA design materials including but not limited to logos, graphics, fonts, colors, and templates for designing printed materials. This resource shall include both original material designed by the NDC as well as materials collected from local chapters. The NDC shall work with the NTC to make this resource easily available for members to access. Be it resolved, the committee shall establish a system for national committees and chapters to request and receive design support in a timely manner. Be it resolved, the committee shall work with relevant parties to revamp the DSA store to provide a wider range of DSA merchandise and be tasked with regularly adding new designs periodically, especially those relevant to national priorities. Be it further resolved, the NPC shall put out an open call for any member in good standing who has skills relevant to the tasks laid out for the National Design Committee to join the committee within 60 days and shall appoint a 5 person steering committee from amongst the applicants to organize and coordinate the committee within 30 days of the opening of the call for members. Be it finally resolved, the National Design Committee shall function as a sub-committee of the National Communications Committee. The chair of the NDC shall work closely with the co-chairs of the Comms Committee to ensure cooperation between the two bodies and to avoid duplicating work. Capacity Commitment & Financial Impact Scores Capacity 3: Moderate to High Finances 3: $10,000 to $50,000 Standing up a National Design Committee and maintaining a robust Design Resource Center will require sustained coordination across multiple bodies, especially to manage design support requests and maintain accessible infrastructure. The merch component adds significant ongoing staff workload—rolling out new designs, managing inventory, and marketing products all demand time and expertise. It is scored 3 for Financial Impact primarily because of the merchandising component, which typically operates at a loss; costs related to production, e-commerce management, inventory, and design tools place the resolution in the moderate financial outlay range. External links Original forum submission: https://discussion.dsausa.org/t/43095 R30: Fighting Back in the Class War: Preparing for May Day 2028[17] Submitted by Will B (Chicago), Sarah H (Chicago). Qualified on May 5, 2025, with 327 signatures as of May 11, 2025. Status: Adopted, as amended Summary This resolution lays out a political vision and tasks for DSA to orient around in the leadup to May Day 2028. Full text Whereas, Shawn Fain and the UAW have called for working people across the US to make May 1, 2028 a day of major labor action that has galvanized working class people nationwide; and Whereas, while a nationwide general strike is unlikely to happen on that date, it is a rare opportunity to have a set future date for class struggle that many working class people and working class institutions are at least rhetorically committed to, and Whereas, organizing towards May Day 2028 provides us a concrete opportunity to build rank and file class consciousness, cross-union organization, popular support, and renewed ties between the socialist movement and the labor movement; and Whereas, building towards May Day 2028 is the kind of national project, like M4A, Bernie, and Strike Ready, that can unify members and chapters in very different circumstances and can be adapted to a wide variety of conditions; and Whereas, DSA has a crucial role to play in moving towards and shaping May Day 2028 in a way that gets the working class in motion and builds working class consciousness, organization, and power Therefore be it resolved, DSA will adopt the following political orientation toward organizing to May Day 2028 1. Political Vision and Strategy. Rather than simply being an amalgam of a variety of individual contract campaigns, unified by a similar expiration date, May Day 2028 must be a moment of mass class consciousness and class action. 1. Over the next three years, DSA will dramatically expand working class consciousness and organization so that, come May Day 2028, the working class can take action to demand a political transformation. This means that we must not only build the organization to get people in motion over the next three years, but also craft the political vision of what that day can be. Our vision of May Day 2028 is the collective action of workers across the country in pursuit of a democratically-determined set of central demands. We must go beyond calling for mass action to lay the foundations and build the structures to make it possible. DSA will help bring together working class leaders to discuss and plan in a structured way, develop an ideological framework and resources to popularize May Day 2028, recruit and develop shop floor militants ahead of May 2028 labor activity, and serve as the home for the millions of as-yet-unorganized workers who may nevertheless want to organize towards this goal. 2. While segments of organized labor have embraced the task of organizing for May Day 2028, much of the labor movement remain aloof from the possibility of coordinated action. DSA, with thousands of members embedded in their unions and their workplaces, is uniquely suited to organize the working class towards May Day 2028 and to bring their unions along with them. We will seek opportunities to work with union leadership where our goals and tasks align, but our focus and priority will be to organize the rank and file of the labor movement and the broader working class ahead of May Day 2028. Not only is that what we, as a mass organization, are best suited for, it is also a recognition that the power of organized labor lies with the rank and file. A union’s membership can move its leadership on a political question far more easily than vice versa. 3. The success of May Day 2028 will depend less on the best laid plans of labor movement top brass and more on the degree to which rank and file workers in and out of unions take initiative themselves. That in turn depends on our ability to publicize both the call for the general strike and effective instances of rank and file participation; provide resources and coaching for rank and file workers who want to find ways to participate with their co-workers; and creative efforts to link immediate shopfloor concerns to broader political demands. Be it further resolved that DSA will commit to pursuing to following actions between now and May 1st 2028: 2. Maintaining a Strategic Vision 1. DSA’s National Labor Commission will continue to collectively develop an analysis of which areas of the economy and labor movement are the most strategic places for DSA members to get involved. 2. This analysis will be done with an eye to where DSA and its members can have the biggest impact on orienting the labor movement and working class towards mass action for May Day 2028 3. Chapters and chapter labor formations will be encouraged to engage in the NLC’s collective analysis and to develop their own analysis of local labor conditions, considering their area’s major industries, employers, and unions, the relationship between the political terrain and the public sector, and any major contracts set to expire over the next three years. 3. Unified DSA Preparation 1. DSA will coordinate among chapters and national bodies to ensure that our efforts and resources are used in a unified way to prepare for May Day 2028. 2. A National May Day 2028 Committee (MD28) will be established to do this coordinating work. 3. DSA will aim to anchor a May Day Convention in late 2026 or early 2027, in concert with major unions that have taken up May Day 2028 as a priority, of unions and other organizations, with a priority on rank and file representation, with the purpose of collectively establishing a plan and set of demands for May Day 2028. 4. Embedding in the Labor Movement 1. DSA will continue to encourage members to get jobs in strategic workplaces, industries, and unions, either as a part of a short- to medium-term salting effort or as a long-term commitment to becoming a shop floor militant. 2. DSA will provide members interested in getting strategic jobs support, including through national programs like Workers Organizing Workers and through chapter-level jobs pipeline programs. 3. DSA will support its members in organizing on the shop floor. Shop floor organizing should start with the concrete issues workers are facing, and ideally should ultimately connect those issues to a broader set of demands and fights that can unite workers nationwide for May Day 2028. 4. DSA members are encouraged to organize around May Day 2028 in their unions. This will look different depending on particular circumstances, but this might include passing a resolution to create a May Day Committee in their union to organize the membership in advance of 2028, lining up contracts to expire on or around May Day 2028, and organizing political education and political discussion events around their union’s political action, cross-union solidarity, and May Day 2028. 5. DSA chapters and chapter labor formations shall be encouraged to conduct thorough mapping of where their members are concentrated, and promote trainings supported by the NLC and workshops that help rank and file members in less-engaged unions to get engagement in their workplaces. Where capacity allows, chapters and chapter labor formations will be encouraged to hold frequent May Day themed workers circles for rank and file workers to engage their co-workers around actions that advance their power on the job and build out the movement for a general strike. 5. Cross Union Organizing 1. DSA members are encouraged to organize cross-union rank and file networks and spaces to organize for May Day 2028. This can look like groups of rank and file workers and local unions coming together to develop an analysis of local conditions, local demands, and shared work, including but not limited to solidarity, new organizing, ballot measures, and local candidates, to build up our strength and power in the leadup to May Day 2028. It can also include industry-specific networks like the Federal Unionists Network organizing around sectoral issues. 2. DSA will nationally and locally build worker committees for particular strategic employers, industries and unions to coordinate around shared work and support each other in our organizing at work and in our unions. This will help our members organizing in their workplaces and their unions stay with it for the long haul to spend the next 3 years building towards May Day 2028. 6. Labor Solidarity 1. DSA will continue to do the kind of broad labor solidarity work we’ve done locally and nationally, including examples like our Strike Ready Campaign for the UAW’s Big 3 Auto Strike. Our work will prioritize supporting unions at the level of the rank and file to be able to stay on strike one day longer than the boss and will serve as a way to get our members who otherwise aren’t involved in the labor movement engaged in class struggle. By showing workers nearing or actually going on strike the power of class consciousness and class organization, and by giving working class people outside of organized labor an onramp into labor struggle, we will bring the working class together in class struggle as we build towards May Day 2028. 2. We will conduct this work both in our chapters, with local labor formations encouraged to use an analysis of local conditions to figure out what labor struggles they can be most useful in providing solidarity, and in our national organization, building on the work of our Strike Ready campaigns and the Solidarity Captains network. 7. Political Education and Agitation 1. DSA will develop materials for agitation and political education around the need to build class power ahead of May Day 2028. We will produce both materials that can be used in one-on-one organizing and in meetings as well as mass communications materials, including images, short videos, posters and flyers to assist members in having political discussions directly with their coworkers, community, and those they meet at actions. 2. Chapters will use these agitational materials and hold political education events directed at the broader working class, particularly in the aftermath of large actions (e.g. May Day rallies, anti-Trump protests) that can provide a political context for the present moment, a vision for the future, and a theory of change for how we get there. National DSA will, through the NPEC and the MD28, provide materials for chapters to do these events. 8. Tenant Union Involvement 1. Between 2025-2027, the Housing Justice Commission (HJC) in collaboration with the MD28 shall facilitate participation by DSA members in the tenant movement in national organizing trainings, conferences, and other programs aimed at supporting preparations for a May Day 2028. 2. The HJC shall coordinate with chapters to map out the presence of and their relationship with local tenant unions. 3. The HJC shall work with chapters and tenant unions to map out Low Income Housing Tax Credit (LIHTC) properties with expired covenants, or covenants that will be expiring in the next several years in that are prime targets for organizing, and develop LIHTC-specific resources for the Emergency Tenant Organizing Committee. 4. The HJC shall develop draft resolutions for tenant unions to adapt and pass pledging support for May Day 2028 and develop their union's strategy for how they will be involved in labor actions and coalitions that year. 9. Chapter Capacity Development 1. Between 2025-2027, the Growth & Development Committee (GDC) in collaboration with the MD28, and any other relevant bodies as determined by the National Political Committee, shall coordinate chapters to engage in regular structure tests to increase internal strike preparedness, strengthen local coalitions, and develop capacity for supporting local strikes. 2. The GDC shall develop trainings and resources related to mobilizations for May Day as well as other significant dates such as International Women’s Day, Trans Day of Visibility, and other high-turnout annual mobilization dates which engage the multi-racial working class. 3. The GDC shall develop new strategies and tactics based on the Organizing Fairs conducted in Spring 2025 with a goal of engaging a broad range of left-wing and labor organizations in directly recruiting and onboarding new organizers into mass work projects related to building labor, tenant and community organizations. 4. The GDC shall encourage and provide space for chapters to report back via writings and group discussions on their experiences to learn from successes and failures in participating in these coalitions, mobilizations, etc. Capacity Commitment & Financial Impact Scores Capacity 4: High Finances 4: Greater than $50,000 The resolution is ranked a 4 for capacity commitment, as it entails sustained national coordination, deep chapter engagement, and long-term rank-and-file organizing infrastructure. It establishes a new national May Day 2028 Committee, tasks DSA with coordinating strategic labor organizing efforts across chapters, supports member salting and shop floor activity, and calls for a national convention with union partners to plan shared demands and action. It is also ranked a 4 for financial impact, primarily due to the costs associated with convening an additional national convention, producing education and organizing materials, and supporting new programs. Status: Referred to NPC Summary It is standard practice within the Palestinian solidarity movement to avoid using terms which normalize Zionism and the Zionist entity. The IC has been handicapped in recent times by the current NPC from using denormalization terminology in its statements, despite such terms being common among our solidarity partners. This resolution strongly encourages the NPC, NPEC, and IC to use denormalization language, ensuring that the IC can use such terms in the future. Full text Whereas, the apartheid and illegitimate state of Israel has been engaging in an illegal occupation and genocide of Palestine for 77 years since the Nakba, displacing millions and killing hundreds of thousands of Palestinians; And whereas, the terminology commonly used in the media and in public forums regarding the Zionist entity has largely legitimized and normalized the entity and the occupation, deeming it a nation-state equivalent to that of all other; And whereas, Palestinian organizations and our allied Palestinian solidarity partners have consistently called to an end of the normalization of the Zionist entity by changing the terminology used in both public and internal communications; Therefore be it resolved, that the Democratic Socialists of America rejects the normalization of the Zionist entity and reaffirms that it is an illegitimate state engaging in the illegal occupation of Palestine and genocide of the Palestinian people; and Be it further resolved, that the national organs of the Democratic Socialists of America, including but not limited to the National Political Committee, the International Committee, and the National Political Education Committee, shall avoid to the extent possible the use of the terms “Israel” and “State of Israel” for public communications, replacing them with more descriptive terms such as “the illegal Israeli occupation” or “the illegitimate state of Israel,” or with the terms in the next resolve if the organ in question determines one of those terms would be better for use; and Be it further resolved, that the aforementioned organs of the Democratic Socialists of America shall in all internal DSA communications refrain from using the terms “Israel” and “State of Israel,” using instead “Zionist entity” or “the settler-colonial project in Palestine,” and Be it finally resolved, that the aforementioned organs of the Democratic Socialists of America shall, for both public and internal communications, refer to the military which enforces the illegal occupation of Palestine either with descriptive terms or with the terms “Israeli Occupying Forces” or IOF, refraining from using “Israel Defense Forces” or “IDF.” Capacity Commitment & Financial Impact Scores Capacity 1: Minimal Finances 1: Less than $5000 This resolution does not require specific actions from staff or members, resulting in minimal time and financial commitments. Full text English Whereas, immigrant and national minority communities tend to be among the most exploited strata of the working class, and represent a particular target of the far right through Trump’s mass deportations and ICE raids targeting students, Whereas, approximately 43.4 million people (13.7% of the population) in the U.S. speak Spanish as their first language, Whereas, Spanish is the second most spoken language in the U.S. after English, and the U.S. is the second-largest Spanish-speaking country in the world, Whereas, 47.6% of the foreign-born workforce in the U.S. identifies as Hispanic, making them the largest group of foreign-born workers in the country. Whereas, past socialist parties in the U.S., such as the Communist Party USA (CPUSA), at their height of organization & participation fostered the ability for workers to organize and participate in their native languages by developing a multilingual political culture and party newspapers published in over 25 languages, Whereas, immigrants in the 19th and 20th centuries organized Language union movements, Whereas, Zohran Mamdani’s campaign and others have shown the electoral impact that the socialist movement can have by reaching out to immigrant workers, Whereas, the development of capacity for DSA members and DSA as an organization to engage with non-English speaking workers in our organizing is an important step towards making DSA a multilingual organization, Whereas, professional interpretation services are expensive, and socialist organizations in the past were able to succeed through recruiting and developing multilingual organizers and community organizations, Whereas, since January 2024 the Housing Justice Commission (HJC) has run a successful weekly trial program of an English/Spanish Language Exchange, which has helped DSA members across the country improve their Spanish fluency and organizing-related vocabulary, Whereas, the HJC English/Spanish Language Exchange has had success in engaging with tenant unionists who are not DSA members, bringing them closer to our organization, Whereas, DSA members and their tenant unions are building out local language exchange programs, such as the one held by Tenant and Neighborhood Councils in the East Bay, Be it therefore resolved, that the DSA prioritizes building itself as a multilingual organization, starting with Spanish as the second most-spoken language and expanding to others where possible, Be it further resolved, the HJC Language Exchanges shall be chartered as Language Exchange for Organizing Needs (LEON). LEON shall run language exchange programs and work to expand DSAs language diversity and multilingual organizing capacity as listed below, Be it further resolved, DSA shall encourage members to learn Spanish and other languages through LEON by advertising it through all convenient means, including but not limited to: * As a part of onboarding new members into DSA, DSA will ask members what languages they speak, * Membership surveys shall include a question on what languages members speak, and their proficiency level with each, * The list of members who speak languages included in an active language exchange project will be shared with LEON; * Chapters will be encouraged to use member language data to organize local Language Exchange efforts, in coordination with LEON where possible, Be it further resolved, LEON will work to support national DSA, DSA chapters, and tenant and labor organizations with translating campaign literature, statements, and other political documents both through organizing multilingual member translators, and making recommendations for paid translation services and organizing partners, Be it further resolved, LEON shall support chapters in setting up their own Language Exchange projects, first by encouraging groups of members from interested chapters to participate in national Language Exchange together, Be it further resolved, LEON shall aim to build toward the capacity to train members as organizing interpreters and multilingual meeting facilitators, Be it further resolved, LEON will be allocated an annual budget of at least $15,000 to support its efforts, and this money shall be spent on instructional support and curriculum development for Language Exchange projects, support for chapter level exchange and interpretation programs, and resources which expand multilingual capacity such as graphic design programs, Be it further resolved, the International Committee (IC) shall, in coordination with LEON and any other national DSA bodies deemed relevant by the National Political Committee (NPC), identify organizations with which to partner on cross-organization Language Exchanges, Be it further resolved, the NPC is tasked with determining a permanent place for LEON within or as a joint project between relevant commissions or working groups, or within any other structure they determine relevant to this resolutions implementation, Be it further resolved, LEON shall have its leadership appointed by the NPC, by a process chosen by the body LEON is placed under, or by any other process determined by the Convention, from a list of members of LEON who join through a form open to all multilingual DSA members and DSA members learning a language, Be it finally resolved, that until a permanent placing and leadership of LEON is selected, LEON will continue to be housed in the HJC so as to preserve continuity of work and ensure effective implementation of this resolution. Status: Adopted Summary DSA needs to bring together labor unions and other mass organizations into a left-labor coalition to run a Presidential candidate in the 2028 Democratic primary. This coalition should also run a national slate of down-ballot candidates in the 2026 and 2028 elections on a common pro-labor platform. This coalition can lay the foundations for a future worker’s party. Full text Whereas, Donald Trump has returned to the White House, launching unprecedented attacks on democratic institutions, the public sector, marginalized communities, and working people broadly on behalf of the billionaire class, which have fueled greater popular resentment of the current US political and economic order and contributed to a growth in class consciousness. Whereas, the failure of the Democratic Party leadership to seriously resist the Trump administration has galvanized the Democratic base against the party establishment. The Democratic Party's favorability has dropped to record lows, creating new openings for independent political organization. The current political moment demands that DSA work to cohere the working class around a new political opposition movement against both Trumpism and the Democratic Party establishment. Whereas, presidential campaigns present a crucial opportunity for socialists to spread our political vision. They can grow an organization’s membership and deepen its bench of down-ballot electeds. The 2016 and 2020 Bernie Sanders presidential campaigns were the most important factors in the growth of the modern socialist movement and modern DSA. Whereas, the lack of a viable left-wing challenger in the 2024 Democratic presidential primary was extremely detrimental for the left and the working class broadly. DSA was left in the difficult position of critiquing the two candidates of the status quo without organizing workers around our own alternative left candidate as a positive example of our political vision. Whereas, the Zohran Mamdani mayoral campaign shows the opportunity that executive office races present in reaching ordinary people and growing DSA’s profile. The Zohran campaign also shows that more work must be done in theorizing how exactly DSA should relate to a candidate’s campaign and vice versa, how to translate the momentum from a campaign into long-term growth for the organization, and how to coordinate our electeds into a single unified block behind a campaign. Whereas, Senator Bernie Sanders and Congresswoman Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, two of the country's most well-known democratic socialists, have traveled the country to rally support for a new political opposition movement against the Democratic establishment. Sanders has stated he intends "to rally people to get engaged in the political process and run as independents outside of the Democratic Party," and the tour has drawn enthusiastic support from tens of thousands of workers. Whereas, with Congressional Democrats at record low popularity, the upcoming 2026 midterm elections present a unique opportunity for electoral success for DSA and the broader Left. Whereas, the 2028 presidential election presents an important opportunity for DSA and the left more broadly to field a serious challenger. A presidential campaign can grow DSA, raise the profile of our down-ballot candidates, popularize our socialist platform, and amplify class conflict between the Democratic Party’s capitalist donors and its increasingly unified working-class and left voter bases. Whereas, the 2028 election also presents an important opportunity to further the merger of the socialist and labor movements, and lay the foundations for a future left-labor party. With the election season coinciding with Shawn Fain’s 2028 May Day strike wave, socialists have an opportunity to connect the economic struggle of labor with political struggle, channeling the economic demands of labor into a political platform. Resolved, DSA should aspire to build a broad left-labor coalition, composed of labor unions and other mass organizations, which can draft a platform; recruit candidates for federal, state, and local office for the 2026 and 2028 elections; and draft a socialist candidate for the 2028 presidential election. In order to gain real traction and look more like Bernie Sanders’ presidential campaigns than past third-party campaigns, DSA should back a viable candidate in the Democratic presidential primary, such as a nationally known elected official, labor leader, or public figure, who will primarily publicly identify with and promote DSA, socialism, and/or a left-labor coalition rather than the Democratic Party. DSA will advocate for such a coalition to endorse independent and nonpartisan down-ballot candidates as well as candidates running in Democratic primaries. Resolved, DSA shall work to build this coalition as a formal electoral alliance of the working class and the political left in the United States. DSA shall reach out to labor unions, political parties, mass organizations, and notable public figures about forming such a coalition to run a slate of candidates in 2026 and 2028, including a possible presidential candidate. Outreach should prioritize: * Guest organizations represented at the 2025 DSA Convention * Labor unions such as UE, UAW, NNU, SEIU and CWA * Political parties such as the Vermont Progressive Party and the Working Families Party * Democratic Socialist elected officials and public figures, including Bernie Sanders, Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, Rashida Tlaib, and other Squad members Resolved, DSA shall work to align and cohere our allies into a unified federal political coalition through our work on immediate political tasks including coordinating grassroots activism, pressure campaigns and national days of action to oppose and defeat the Trump administration's fascist initiatives. DSA will advocate for expanding the Fighting Oligarchy tour and existing nationwide protests into a sustained campaign of rallies and mobilizations against fascism throughout the duration of the Trump administration, building towards the 2026 and 2028 elections. Resolved, the NPC shall form a multi-tendency exploratory committee tasked with reviewing the lessons of the 2016 and 2020 “DSA for Bernie” campaigns and explore the different possibilities for a 2028 DSA Presidential campaign (including the relative merits of an ‘independent expenditure’ campaign vs. a campaign in direct consultation with the candidate). The committee shall include at least 1 national co-chair, 3 at-large NPC members and 2 representatives from the NEC. The committee shall submit a report to the NPC prior to the 2027 convention. If DSA decides to endorse a candidate for the 2028 Democratic primary, the committee shall draft a consensus resolution outlining the campaign for the 2027 DSA convention. Resolved, DSA shall seek to form a broad left-labor coalition to run a presidential candidate and other federal candidates, but is not precluded from running federal candidates without one. If a labor-left coalition emerges, DSA should advocate for it to continue and grow through the course of the 2028 elections, toward a long-term goal of forming an independent working-class political party. Resolved, the NPC shall appoint DSA’s representatives to any national coalition body. If a coalition that DSA is a member of decides to endorse a presidential candidate, the NPC shall hold a national all-member referendum on whether to endorse that candidate. Resolved, the NPC shall develop a communications plan for DSA to publicly agitate for the creation of a broad alliance of the left and labor in the United States, including an NPC statement, social media communications, and a pamphlet modeled after the Rank and File Strategy and Workers Deserve More pamphlets. Resolved, if there isn't sufficient interest in forming a broad left-labor coalition, DSA should still attempt to endorse a viable and politically aligned presidential candidate. Likewise, if there is no sufficient presidential candidate, DSA should still attempt to cohere a larger left-labor coalition. Capacity Commitment & Financial Impact Scores Capacity 4: High Finances 4: Greater than $50,000 This resolution outlines a multi-year electoral strategy focused on building a national left-labor coalition, with components that may include support for a 2028 presidential campaign, down-ballot candidate recruitment, national mobilizations, and outreach to unions, elected officials, and allied organizations. It calls for the formation of a multi-tendency exploratory committee, the development of a national communications plan, and coordination of national political campaigns. Given the breadth and duration of these activities, the resolution is scored a 4 for Capacity Commitment due to the significant staff coordination and sustained member engagement required across chapters and national bodies. The Financial Impact is also scored a 4, based on projected costs associated with potential presidential campaign activity, production and distribution of national political materials, organizing mobilizations, supporting coalition work, and managing electoral efforts over multiple cycles — with anticipated expenditures reasonably expected to exceed $50,000. Summary Two important events in 2028 – the presidential elections and the labor movement’s response to the UAW call for a May Day strike – present crucial opportunities for mass organizing. DSA must engage with our partners across left, labor, and liberation movements in pursuit of a united front. This resolution convenes a 2028 Planning Committee to liaise across national bodies and build chapter preparedness ahead of 2028, and directs DSA to take incremental steps toward a broad electoral coalition. Full text Whereas, a united front tactic has been instrumental throughout history in fighting fascism and imperialism, and in achieving unprecedented democratic victories for the Left on unfavorable terrain (e.g., the 1967 United Front in West Bengal; the Sigamos Haciendo Historia coalition spearheaded by Morena in Mexico); Whereas, the 2028 presidential election, coming at the end of Trump’s second term and possibly coinciding with a May Day mass strike should the labor movement coalesce behind United Auto Workers (UAW) President Shawn Fain’s call to align contracts, will be a major site of political mobilization that requires that DSA develop an organizational strategy for engagement; Whereas, the uncertainty around the specific opportunities and scenarios we may be faced with in relation to both the election and a potential mass strike require that DSA begin now the process of building chapter preparedness, opening dialogue with other formations, and developing robust analysis around the viability and requirements of different strategies; Whereas, the chances of an insurgent socialist challenger in the Democratic primary are uncertain, and if such a challenger should arise, they will face obstruction by the Democratic Party, which has shown during the 2016 and 2020 Bernie Sanders primary campaigns its willingness to pull any stops to prevent a progressive victory; Whereas, the 2023 DSA National Convention voted to pass the National Electoral Committee Consensus Resolution which, as amended, directed the NEC to “develop programs and strategies to strengthen our already existing organizational independence from the Democratic Party” with the goal of “presenting a third, democratic socialist alternative for working-class people that is organizationally, strategically, and visibly independent of the Democratic Party”; Whereas, should progressive political forces outside the Democratic Party enter into a coalitional collaboration around a unified strategy for the 2028 election, DSA’s participation in such a coalition would significantly strengthen its reach while advancing DSA’s electoral strategy goals as outlined by the 2023 convention; Whereas, a broad Arab, Muslim, youth, immigrant base, and broader sections of the Democratic voter base largely came together in support of Uncommitted, “No Votes For Genocide”, and third-party candidates in the 2024 presidential election with large numbers of abstention in key swing states; Whereas, the 2024 presidential election saw burgeoning collaboration between progressive third party campaigns entering vote-swap agreements with each other; Whereas, building alternative electoral coalitions with other Left and progressive forces entrenches bases disillusioned with the dual-party system and the Democratic Party, and builds up infrastructure for strategic independent local, state, and federal races. Therefore, be it resolved, DSA shall make it a priority to explore building and supporting a broad Left-Labor coalition through the two agitational organizing opportunities offered by the 2028 presidential elections and the possibility of a May Day 2028 general strike; Be it resolved, the National Political Committee shall begin the process of entering into direct regular dialogue with other political organizations, including, but not limited to, political parties, labor unions, tenant unions, social movements and other organizations aligned with our values (in particular, immigrant, abolitionist, and Palestinian diaspora organizations), in the pursuit of coalition building; Be it resolved, the NPC shall work to advance and agitate around strategic demands from the “Workers Deserve More” platform in meetings with coalitional partners about May Day 2028 and the 2028 Presidential election; DSA members shall also work to establish the “Workers Deserve More” platform through local union participation and local electoral campaigns; Be it resolved, by the end of 2025, the NPC shall convene a 2028 Planning Committee comprised of one liaison each from the NEC, NLC, YDSA NCC; the two NPC co-chairs; as well as 6 at-large members selected by the NPC by Single Transferable Vote from an application process open to all DSA members in good standing; Be it resolved, the NPC shall strive for demographic and geographical representation on the committee, with a minimum of one representative of each major region of the United States, gender diversity, and inclusion of Black, brown, and immigrant members; and prioritizing members with a history of chapter- or national-level electoral or labor organizing, and/or who occupy leadership roles in their respective chapters; Be it resolved, the 2028 Planning Committee shall develop proposals for an independent coalitional electoral strategy at the national and local level, including the 2028 Presidential Election, by researching: * A list of other socialist formations, progressive parties and organizations, and labor unions that might be willing to engage in such an electoral coalition (e.g. the Party for Socialism and Liberation (PSL), the Working Families Party (WFP), the Green Party, United Auto Workers (UAW), United Electrical, Radio and Machine Workers of America (UE), and others); * The administrative viability of DSA obtaining ballot access independent of the Democratic Party and/or sharing ballot access with other coalition partners; * The strategy employed by insurgent progressive electoral coalitions around the world (e.g., Morena in Mexico and the New Popular Front in France), including similarities and differences in political conditions and actors (e.g., role of labor or lack thereof); Be it resolved, the 2028 Planning Committee shall direct the NEC to form a subcommittee tasked with: * Providing direct assistance to local chapters that are interested in exploring ballot access for local races, including in coalition with other political organizations within their jurisdictions, and helping facilitate statewide coordination between chapters exploring ballot access; * Supporting chapters interested in pursuing ballot access to run independent candidates in 2026 as a structure test through field guidance and national resources; * Produce resources to help chapters achieve filing deadlines, collect signatures, and meet other ballot access requirements; Be it resolved, the 2028 Planning Committee shall bring a proposal based on the previous research, structure tests, and shifting material conditions of the national political landscape to the 2027 DSA National Convention for an organizational strategy for 2028. The Financial Impact score of 4 reflects the substantial costs associated with organizing national coalitions, supporting ballot access campaigns, producing resources, and hosting strategic convenings. Qualified on May 6, 2025, with 276 signatures as of May 11, 2025. Status: Adopted Summary This resolution would enshrine the Workers Deserve More Program as DSA’s platform. It also creates a committee to propose edits based on political commitments made by delegates at convention to the NPC, coordinate a public campaign to popularize Workers Deserve More using digital, press, print, video and social media interventions, and create political education training events to ensure WDM is incorporated into chapter campaigns and DSA elected officials’ platforms. Full text Whereas: Socialist and labor parties throughout the world have political programs that analyze history and political economy, put forward a coherent vision of the world they are fighting for, immediate demands to help get there, and a strategy to achieve both. These are written in a language accessible to broad layers of people outside the organizations and often include design elements that are transferable across mediums and easily recognizable. DSA’s organizational strategy has long included the promotion of some form of “Where We Stand” document or “platform” that explains what DSA is and what we are trying to do, versions of which are on our website and in many of our chapters’ bylaws. The resolution “Defending Democracy Through Political Independence” passed in 2023 resulted in the formation of a multi-tendency “For Our Rights Campaign Committee” (FORC) which successfully produced the short program “Workers Deserve More” (WDM) for 2024, outlining DSA’s current and evergreen political and social stances and demands in readable, attractive prose and artwork. Since the task of writing WDM was completed, FORC has been dissolved. Chapters and priority committees across DSA have found the printed booklet and the online version of WDM invaluable organizing tools to advertise DSA to newcomers, educate and orient new members, and as a guide for debate and deliberation among active members, and have innovated various short versions (eg palm cards) and digital media to further the WDM message and represent DSA as an independent political organization. The 2025 convention is the occasion for our organization to pass our 2025-27 agendas and elect our new leadership, and until the entire convention is over and any changes to our priorities are tallied and published, DSA does not know what a current program reflecting our political growth and what we have committed to setting forward ought to contain. Be it resolved: “Workers Deserve More” will remain the name of DSA’s program indefinitely, replacing all other organizational documents that represent our national platform and “Where We Stand” except within chapter bylaws, which may be amended according to the discretion of chapter members. The current WDM will stand as DSA’s political position statement until a new WDM is created to replace it. Future conventions retain the right to change the name of the political program. The NPC will hold an application period immediately after the new NPC is seated, starting in 2025 and ending 30 days thereafter, for an 13 member Program committee. The makeup of the Program committee will be: * one member of the GDC steering committee * one member of the IC steering committee * one member of the NEC steering committee * one member of the NLC steering committee * one member of the NPEC steering committee * four members of the NPC, including one YDSA co-chair and one DSA co-chair * four at-large members in good standing and will be approved and seated by the full NPC within two weeks of the conclusion of the application period. Committee members will be elected by the relevant bodies and submitted for NPC approval, and NPC and at-large members will be elected by the NPC via STV. The Program committee will then elect 2 co-chairs. The tasks of the Program committee will be to: * assess all the political commitments delegates made at convention, and propose WDM edits to the NPC to clearly and accurately reflect priorities, demands, continuities and new perspectives in a document that generally matches the length and prose style of WDM. * submit this document by December 1 of the same year for NPC approval * roll out a month long public national campaign to unveil the new WDM by February 1 of the year after convention, with digital, press, print, video and audio interventions, with support from the National Tech Committee, Democratic Left/Socialist Forum, the National Communications Committee and our national staff, as well as DSA-endorsed elected officials wherever possible * create and implement political education sessions and training to support rank and file members, DSA leaders, and DSA-endorsed electeds in the adaptation and use of WDM across our campaign and priority committees and chapters, in collaboration with the Democracy Commission and our national staff. The rollout of these sessions and training will begin by February 1 across the country, to take place relatively simultaneously over the course of a month. All curricular materials will be made available to DSA’s members in good standing. * oversee the distribution of WDM pamphlets to chapters, campaign committees, and the DSA store. After these tasks are completed, the Program committee will dissolve and the NPC members who had been on the committee will be primary liaisons and stewards to the organization’s various bodies and socialists in office to support and promote the effective use of WDM. In order to receive a national endorsement, electoral candidates will be expected to accept and promote DSA’s program, and align their own campaign platforms with its contents to the best of their ability. Summary This resolution establishes a political program for DSA, expressing our analysis of capitalism in the US and outlining clear fighting demands for our organization to rally around which will provide guidance for our political work and will enable us to win over critical layers of the working class through active campaigning and organizing to attain them. Full text A resolution for a program for the Democratic Socialists of America to be adopted at the 2025 DSA National Convention. Whereas in order to build a new society, our organization must have unity around our goals and beliefs and an ability to explain our politics to people in our lives and communities. Whereas historical socialist parties have developed unity by adopting a program which explains capitalist society, includes demands which connect to present consciousness, and clearly states that the working class will need to conquer political power. Whereas although DSA passed a platform in 2021 and a program for the 2024 elections, DSA has not adopted a clear and precise general program yet. Whereas while DSA remains a broad-tent embracing a diversity of socialist tendencies, a DSA program must clearly explain how we will end the capitalist state and place the working class in control of society; Therefore be it resolved, that DSA will adopt a political program to replace both the 2021 Platform and Workers Deserve More to be the basis of political unity with the organization and to provide an explanation of our political aims to the working class; and Resolved, that DSA's program will be posted prominently on our website and on other materials, included in new member materials, and will be distributed widely among both our membership and the wider working class; and Resolved, that the program so adopted may only be changed at a DSA National Convention; and Resolved, that a Program Coordinating Committee will be established and tasked with promoting chapter use of the program; and Resolved, that Program Coordinating Committee will be further tasked with assisting chapters in adapting an immediate program to local and tactical conditions, providing a practical bridge between the struggles chapters engage in and the long-term political struggle waged by DSA; and Resolved, that DSA adopts the following as its program: POLITICAL PROGRAM OF THE DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS OF AMERICA We live in a country run by a class of bosses and billionaires called capitalists. They have bought and run the Democratic and Republican parties, most news outlets, colleges and universities, and every branch of government from city halls to the Senate. They use their power to exploit the vast majority who work to live—the hundreds of millions of us who make up the working class. This system can only be ended by the working class taking political power from the rich and building a new society. We in the Democratic Socialists of America fight for that society: a democratic socialist society. Our wages are stagnant, our hours are long, and prices are only growing higher. We increasingly live paycheck to paycheck, one bad day away from financial ruin. And yet it is our labor that powers this unjust system. The capitalists who own the businesses we work at take all the profits for themselves and use them to control our society. This is the exploitation that defines the capitalist system. The capitalist system exploits Black, immigrant, and Indigenous people by dividing them from the rest of the working class. Millions of people of color face discrimination, unemployment, and police violence, locking them out of political power and an equal quality of life. Oppressive laws restricting abortion, marriage, and self-expression force women and queer people to choose between being controlled by their family or living in poverty outside of it. Different people face different kinds of oppression, but as members of the working class we all want to control the direction of our lives. Every law, policy, or practice that oppresses us for who we are stems from the capitalists’ control over our society and reinforces it. We all have a common interest against the capitalist bosses: their rule threatens our freedom and safety. To be able to defeat the ruling class and end their exploitation of our labor, we need to fight the oppression every working person faces in this country. No matter their race, gender, or sexual orientation, we stand side by side. Capitalism is a global system that exploits workers around the world. The most powerful capitalists use their wealth to influence governments into waging wars, toppling other governments, and starving entire peoples with sanctions and embargoes. They use this power to coerce other countries into selling their natural resources, labor, and goods for cheap prices. This imperialist exploitation forces workers of wealthy and poor countries to compete in a race to the bottom. The United States has become a superpower through exploiting and oppressing countries throughout the Middle East, Latin America, Asia, and Africa while crushing and bribing workers at home. As workers in the most powerful country on the planet, we must build a global movement against the exploitation of the working class by opposing our government's imperialist goals and toppling its capitalist backers. Both political parties work for the capitalist class in a political system rigged to keep the ruling class in charge. The working class needs a party of its own to change this. We need an organization by and for our class, where our politicians reflect our values and where we make our decisions democratically. Democratic Socialists of America is that party. We are united by a program of putting workers in control. In our fight against oppression and exploitation, we sit with our neighbors on rent strikes, stand with unions in strikes to win better pay and benefits, protest oppression, and feed our communities. We elect our own members to legislatures around the country to speak out against injustices while fighting for healthcare and cheap groceries. Winning reforms or building a mass workers’ party alone is not enough. The Constitution is written to protect the rich few from the working majority. Anything we win from the rich can be taken away with the stroke of a pen. The historic victories of the labor movement, the New Deal, and the Civil Rights movement are already being stripped away. In order to protect our victories and implement the wider changes we need, the working class must take political power from the rich and create a new republic based on a democratic constitution. But winning the battle for democracy is just the start of the fight. The capitalist class will fight back tooth and nail with their control of industries and money. If we want a government by and for workers to stand a chance, we must immediately use political power to seize control of key industries and finance. We will replace the secret deliberations of a few shareholder boards with public, democratic control at every level of the economy. We will have a socialist society where economic prosperity will serve our needs instead of profit. The future of our country and the future of humanity will be decided by which class rules: capitalists or workers. Democratic Socialists of America is dedicated to overthrowing the capitalists’ dictatorship and establishing a democratic socialist government. What We Fight for Today DSA fights all over the country for policies that will improve the lives of working people today. These policies alone will not end the unjust system we live under, but we believe that by fighting the bosses for things working people need now, we can build a movement that can eventually take power and build a government of working people. 1. End the Deportations: ICE’s deportations are a weapon used to oppress the working class and must end immediately. Abolish ICE and end the exploitation of migrant workers. 2. Stop the Genocide: Free Palestine. We call for an immediate and permanent ceasefire in Gaza. End support for the state of Israel, including military support, weapons sales, the targeting of pro-Palestinian activists, and tax incentives for Israeli bonds. 3. Lower the Prices: People are struggling to make ends meet. The cost of living must go down. Essential goods like food, water, and energy must be made affordable by controlling the prices directly. 4. Jobs for All: A good job is a human right. We demand the minimum wage be increased to $20 an hour, a 32 hour workweek, and a jobs program guaranteeing everyone in this country a living wage. 5. Medicare for All: Nobody should be afraid of going bankrupt due to a medical emergency. We demand the cancellation of all medical debt and a universal health care system that includes abortion and gender-affirming care. 6. Housing is a Human Right: Nobody should sleep on the streets. Freeze rents and evictions, and allow tenants to collectively bargain. Create universally accessible social housing by redistributing housing hoarded by landlords. 7. Democratic Elections: Our elections are undemocratic, with an unrepresentative Senate, gerrymandered House districts, restrictions on voting rights, and unaccountable money spent by SuperPACs. We fight for voting rights for all, ending the Electoral College, public campaign finance, and proportional representation. 8. Fight Oppressive Laws: We fight for sanctuary cities and oppose every oppressive or discriminatory law. We are fighting to end all legal and political oppression against people for their race, gender, sexual orientation, immigration status, disability, and more. DSA stands for new rights and laws protecting the oppressed. 9. Protect the Environment: Corporations must not destroy the environment for their profits. Environmental regulations must be enforced to protect our communities. We fight for a Green New Deal to begin investing in green energy, infrastructure, and build free public transportation with a just transition for every worker. 10. A Union For Every Worker: Dignity at work is a fundamental right. We call for a mass new organizing campaign by the largest trade unions, and demand a government which protects the right for workers to organize and gives federal workers the right to strike. We are fighting and building unions to organize every worker in a powerful, democratic union. Winning a Socialist Republic Democratic Socialists of America fights today for things like universal health care, jobs for all, and ending oppression. But we do not limit ourselves to individual reforms— we fight to create a new society. Doing that will require a mass movement of the working class, ready to decisively defeat the capitalists and end their rule over society. Democratic Socialists of America puts forward the following program to end capitalist dictatorship and begin building a socialist society: 1. A Democratic Socialist Republic: We are fighting for the working class to conquer power from the capitalists, smash their oppressive state, and create a government controlled by the working class. We are fighting to build a working class democracy, a socialist society without the racist prison and police system where we will finally be able to live as equals. 1. Abolish the Presidency and the Senate, and place supreme political power in a working class democracy consisting of a unicameral legislature, workers’ councils, and popular assemblies. 2. Guarantee freedom of speech, protest, organizing, and the right to strike. 3. Require all elections to be conducted proportionally. 4. Provide universal citizenship for residents and guarantee freedom of movement through our borders. 5. Replace existing law enforcement agencies with a public safety force run by local communities for de-escalation and protecting democratic and social rights. Ban former officers from joining and eliminate qualified immunity. 6. Guarantee full rights for people under trial and rehabilitation, and transform prisons into public facilities for rehabilitation and re-entering society. End all forms of prison slavery. 7. Enshrine the right to abortion, receive reproductive care, and the right to form families regardless of marriage or blood relation. 2. A Workers’ Economy: A mass workers’ movement for political power must immediately place the economy under the control of the working class. With democracy in our workplaces, schools, and neighborhoods, we can leverage prosperity to build a good life for everyone. 1. Nationalize large corporations, transportation, and essential industries, replacing the shareholder boards with public workers councils drawn from unions and accountable to working class democracy. 2. Provide quality housing, food, education, water, family care, and other fundamental necessities of life to all residents. Support the creation of public spaces and art. 3. Guarantee universal healthcare for all, free at point of service. Coverage will include disability care, gender-affirming care, and reproductive healthcare. 4. End the segregation and exploitation of Black people and other people of color. Use the wealth of the rich to pay reparations and build their communities. 5. Nationalize all utilities and build a national power grid using solar, wind, and other clean energy technologies in place of fossil fuels. Secure a just transition to a sustainable economy and respect planetary boundaries. 6. Centralize infrastructure and provide free public transit across the country, including expanded regional and high-speed electric rail. 3. An End to Empire: A socialist government will end foreign wars and the war against oppressed people at home, end the United States’ part in the exploitation of the international working class, and pursue a just transition for the majority of defense workers towards work which serves all of humanity. 1. Limit the military to self-defense, public infrastructure, and disaster relief, with its leadership accountable to working class democracy. Guarantee civilian rights and residence during military service. 2. Grant all nations and colonies within the United States the right to determine their destiny, including separation or joining the republic. 3. Guarantee right of return to Indigenous nations based on historic treaties or adaptations by their democratic representatives. 4. Close all overseas military bases, end our occupations of other countries and bring our military home, end trade in weapons, dismantle all secret agencies, and grant immunity and protection for whistleblowers. 5. End sanctions and economic strong-arming of other countries. 6. End all economic and military support for states engaged in apartheid or genocide. 7. Share research, resources, and technology needed to build an interconnected, global energy infrastructure powered completely by clean, renewable energy sources. Resolved, the section of the program entitled "What We Fight For Today" is adopted until the 2027 National Convention, when the Program Coordinating Committee will provide an update for the National Convention within its consensus proposal. Qualified on May 6, 2025, with 305 signatures as of May 11, 2025. Status: Adopted Summary This resolution instructs the NPC to implement more stipends for elected leaders in next year’s budget. National leaders are almost all unpaid, which makes it very difficult to spend the time necessary to lead politically! We want our national leaders to come from a variety of backgrounds, not just white collar professionals or high income earners who have relatively more free time. Full text Whereas: DSA has long made a practice of paying elected members to lead the organization, including full-time salaries for National Co-Chairs, part-time stipends for YDSA Co-Chairs, part-time stipends for YDSA National Coordinating Committee members (until 2025), part-time stipends for NPC Steering Committee members (until 2025), and full-time salaries for National Labor Commission Co-Chairs (approved by the 2023 Convention but not implemented). Whereas: Salaries and stipends for members are a common practice in unions and parties around the world because they allow elected leaders to carry out a political mandate while under democratic oversight, which is much less feasible when an organization relies exclusively on unpaid member labor, unelected staff, and outside consultants. Whereas: Salaries and stipends for elected members strengthen the working-class character of DSA because they allow people to lead who otherwise would not have time due to work or other economic constraints. Otherwise, socialist leaders will disproportionately come from circumstances that tend to naturally have more flexibility and freedom, such as high-income families, white-collar professions, and personal lives without children or caregiving responsibilities. Whereas: In discussing how to implement paid political leadership, some members of the Democracy Commission expressed the difficulty of making a recommendation because of practical considerations around the budget, and this resolution addresses that. Resolved: This resolution re-affirms the commitments made at previous conventions to enact paid political leadership in national DSA. Resolved: Unless the NPC makes an affirmative finding by majority vote that the funds are not available for budget year 2026, the NPC will implement additional part-time stipends for member-leadership roles in the 2026 budget. In case of a finding of lack of funds, the NPC will publish and carry out a savings and fundraising plan to implement those stipends in the following year. In this process, the NPC will prioritize part-time stipends for Communications Chair or Co-Chairs, the NPC Steering Committee, and National Labor Commission Co-Chairs. Resolved: Stipends equivalent to half-time wages or higher shall only be implemented for NPC members or positions that have been elected by a vote of the most recent national convention delegates, either at convention or subsequently. Resolved: Before creating a new staff position, the NPC will first consider whether the work could be done by elected or appointed members, either on a paid or unpaid basis. Status: Adopted Summary Solidarity with the Palestinian people obligates us to be targeted, unified, and unwavering in our commitment to build the BDS Movement. This resolution offers a cohesive DSA strategy to fulfill these obligations while building a stronger organization and a stronger movement. Full text Whereas, as democratic socialists living in the heart of the U.S. empire, we have a responsibility to follow the leadership of oppressed people in their struggles against harm perpetrated by the United States government. Whereas, the BDS Movement represents the largest majority of Palestinian civil society composed of over 170 parties, unions, and other organizations, and has explicitly called upon international organizations to impose boycotts and divestment initiatives against Israel. Whereas, the BDS National Committee formed in Ramallah in 2007 has the mandate to formulate strategies in accordance with the 2005 BDS Call and serve as the Palestinian-led reference point for global BDS campaigns. Whereas, DSA endorsed the BDS movement at its 2017 national convention and enshrined our support into the platform passed at the 2021 convention. Whereas, in the most recent escalation of the U.S. Israeli genocide of the Palestinian people since October 7th, 2023, DSA both nationally and at the chapter level have led and participated in a variety of political interventions for Palestine including No Money for Massacres, local ceasefire resolutions, labor organizing for a ceasefire, municipal divestment campaigns, the Uncommitted Movement, the March on the DNC, YDSA-led university divestment, and nationally coordinated Boycott Chevron work. Whereas, this work has ultimately been unsuccessful as Israel’s genocide with US support continues with impunity. Whereas, ending the complicity of states, corporations, and institutions in Israel’s ongoing genocide against 2.3 million Palestinians in Gaza is the most effective form of solidarity with the Palestinian struggle to end the genocide and dismantle Israel’s 76-year-old regime of settler-colonialism and apartheid. Whereas, only targeted strategic campaigns that focus on mass organizing and orienting to the largest sections of the working class can build the power to force the U.S government, institutions and corporations to end their complicity in Israeli genocide, apartheid and occupation. Whereas, DSA chapters across the country are engaging in various BDS campaigns, but DSA currently has no universal or formal support infrastructure to track and support BDS organizing across DSA chapters and national bodies outside of limited attempts such as the International Committee’s StopFuelingGenocide campaign. Therefore be it resolved, DSA reaffirms our unwavering solidarity with the Palestinian people in the struggle against Zionist settler colonization, Israeli apartheid, and US Imperialism, Be it further resolved, DSA understands our primary responsibility as a US based organization in the heart of empire is to force our government and institutions to end their complicity through boycotts, divestments, and sanctions, as called for by the largest portions of Palestinian Civil Society in 2005 and represented by the BDS National Committee, and DSA commits to supporting the BDS movement in all aspects of our work. Be it further resolved, DSA nationally will engage in the broadest coalitions possible to further Palestine solidarity organizing while limiting deeper partnerships to organizations that endorse the BDS movement and support the three demands outlined in its introductory call: ending Israeli occupation and colonization of all Arab lands and dismantling the Wall; recognizing the fundamental rights of the Arab-Palestinian citizens of Israel to full equality; and respecting, protecting and promoting the rights of Palestinian refugees to return to their homes and properties as stipulated in UN Resolution 194. Be it further resolved, DSA chapters are encouraged to participate in coalition with other organizations in their communities including but not limited to grassroots Palestinian activist organizations, labor unions, tenants unions, and religious organizations. Be it further resolved, DSA will prioritize campaigns targeting (1) institutions including but not limited to universities, city/town/state governments, and pension funds and (2) corporate pressure campaigns targeting companies including but not limited to Chevron and Maersk. Be it further resolved, the DSA International Committee is tasked with creating and maintaining an expansive chapter tracking and training infrastructure for local Palestine solidarity organizing. Be it further resolved, the IC will be responsible for generating an annual report of chapter Palestine solidarity activities to be published to membership. Be it further resolved, chapter training will revolve around building sustainable BDS campaigns and using campaign work to build strong chapters. These trainings should be given both in the form of national calls as well as one on one mentorship with the leaders of chapters. Topics for these trainings should include but are not limited to: * The Organizing Cycle * The “Labor Notes Bullseye” * Listwork * Power mapping * Campaign Escalation * Effective Comms Strategies * Press Relations * Info Security * Protest Safety Be it further resolved, the International Committee and YDSA will collaborate on shared campaigns and actions with overlapping targets such as Chevron. Be it further resolved, DSA International Committee will work with YDSA to create resources to help support DSA chapters and organizers in their work supporting student activism such as the “How DSA can support the Student Revolution for Gaza” Emergency Meeting held on 04/28/24. Be it further resolved, DSA chapters are directed to support campus-based BDS work through the mobilization and organization of broader community and worker support. Be it further resolved, that the National Labor Committee (NLC) will assist the International Committee in providing training to chapters on how to best establish relationships with organized labor with the goal of increasing labor’s support to aforementioned BDS campaigns targeting institutions and companies. Be it further resolved, the NLC shall complete a mapping of DSA union members and, in consultation with the IC, identify strategic targets including leveraging support to external campaigns such as municipal divestment and launching internal campaigns to divest union funds from Israeli apartheid and genocide. Be it further resolved, the NLC will create training and resources for union members to organize for Palestine. Be it further resolved, the National Electoral Commission (NEC) will be responsible for identifying opportunities for state and local pro-Palestine legislation as modeled off of Zohran Mamdani’s “Not on Our Dime” bill in the NY State government. Be it further resolved, DSA organizing will prioritize campaigns focused on intersectional targets that are relevant to different struggles and DSA organizing bodies such as immigrant justice organizing against Palantir in collaboration with the International Migrants working group of the International Committee and Housing Justice organizing against Airbnb in collaboration with the Housing Justice Commission. Be it further resolved, the National Communications Committee (NCC) will work with the IC to highlight chapter’s Palestine Campaigns, especially chapter victories. The NCC will also work with the IC to create informational graphics, short form videos, and visual statements about the work that chapters are engaged in, the conditions within Palestine, and DSA’s political perspective on those conditions. Be it further resolved, the Democratic Left Editorial Board is requested to publish a monthly piece of content related to DSA organizing for Palestine to be included in the monthly NPC newsletter when feasible. Be it further resolved, DSA will host an in-person national conference for DSA Palestine organizers to discuss Palestine solidarity strategy in 2026. If an independent conference is deemed infeasible by the NPC, the organization will aim to plan a single day or simultaneous gathering appended to a YDSA National event, Socialism Conference, or a similar national event. These costs are expected to fall within the $5,001–$10,000 range, reflecting limited but notable expenditures that go beyond routine administrative support.
